params.system:
You are an independent expert referee assessing the SHARPNESS of mathematical results in a research project on the
asymptotic theory of a sequential Monte Carlo method for Bayesian variable selection (linear regression, p <= n^A, often
p >> n). Every result is asymptotic; finite-n behaviour is not a defect. The project's main risk is publishing theorems
that are correct but weaker than what is achievable.

You receive the working files of one ticket and a list of headline claims located by file and line span. Ignore any
status, score or review verdict the files assert. Take each claim as correct; your job is NOT to re-check the proof.

For each claim assess:
(a) hypotheses: is any assumption stronger than the proof needs (say which weaker condition suffices, with the step
    where it is used), or is it necessary (give a counterexample or a known lower bound showing that)?
(b) conclusion: is the rate, constant regime, scaling range (e.g. the exponent range for p vs n, beta-min level, sparsity
    growth) or mode of convergence improvable? Compare with the best known results for Bayesian variable selection
    (e.g. Johnson-Rossell, Narisetty-He, Castillo-Schmidt-Hieber-van der Vaart, Yang-Wainwright-Jordan MCMC mixing,
    Song-Liang, Zhou-Yang-Chang-Liang); cite only results you are confident about, and say when you are unsure.
(c) the cheapest concrete route to a stronger version, if one exists, and how hard it looks.

Severity: SHARP = no improvement you can justify; IMPROVABLE-EASY = a stronger version follows with a modest change you
can describe; IMPROVABLE-HARD = a stronger version is plausible or known elsewhere but needs new work; UNCLEAR = cannot
judge from the material.

Output, in this order:
1. For each claim, a short section: claim id, the assessment (a)-(c) with exact locations (file:line).
2. Then exactly one line per claim, nothing after the last one:
SHARP <claim id> VERDICT=<SHARP|IMPROVABLE-EASY|IMPROVABLE-HARD|UNCLEAR>

   1| # W3-SAMP · REPORT to Theory HQ (PROGRAM item 4: sampler outputs as coded, honestly labelled)
   2| 
   3| **Flags at the top.**

   5| 2. **Code finding:** main (4676af6) computes **no plain (endpoint) PIP**. The only PIP it reports is the Rao–Blackwell

  15| ## 1. RESULT
  16| 
  17| **PROVED-CHECKED.** All of the following hold for every result in the package:
  18| - a proof file exists;
  19| - the statement was locked (SL1);
  20| - the sharpness gate ran (ASSUMPTION_MAP + boundary numerics + the better-theorem review BT1);

  31| ## 2. The statement as proved
  32| 
  33| File: `STATEMENT.md` (v3). It is about the method as coded on main and is design-agnostic.
  34| 
  35| Two conventions run through every claim:
  36| - Finite-sample claims are given the data and the calibration record 𝓒, on 𝒜, in W1-N1's localised form. In code terms,
  37|   𝒜 = {SMC branch and calibration status "ok", including the tier-1 fallback}.

  39|   {completed} ⊆ 𝒜 (reported outputs). P(𝒜) → 1 is never assumed.
  40| - Joint-law idealisation (STATEMENT.md §0): the final streams 10–13 are idealised as independent of the data as well

  42|   D, LT, C and TR relies on this idealisation, not on separate marginal-independence claims.

  44| Results:
  45| 
  46| - **Lemma CC (code facts).**
  47|   - Every π₀ draw is scored and offered to the HPM ledger before its accept decision. This covers the initial draws and
  48|     the one independence proposal per particle per round, accepted or rejected.
  49|   - Each island makes exactly D_r = N_e(1+T+L+4) draws.
  50|   - The reported HPM is the best model, under the coded strict order, of everything the final run's ledger was offered.
  51|   - pip_primary is the equal-weight mean of the island RB PIPs; MPM = {pip_primary > ½}; log_Z = log of the mean Ẑ_r.
  52|   - In production, T ≤ 4·max(1000, ⌈log₂(n+p+1)⌉²) and B ≤ 16.
  53|   - Every sampler function an island can reach is unchanged from N1's code of record. The differences are the removed
  54|     plain-PIP writes, plus the LS0 start-mode code and event labels outside the island.
  55| - **Lemma PC.** On completed runs, each island's records and its evaluated-model set equal those of the uninterrupted
  56|   run. The reported HPM is the maximum of the whole ledger: islands, tables, inherited models, final search and LS0.
  57| - **Theorem D (draw discovery, item d).**
  58|   - The probability that no draw of an island equals S₀ is exactly (1 − π₀(S₀))^{D_r}. Under IND-T the exponent is 4D_r.
  59|   - P(completed ∩ {Ŝ ≠ S₀}) ≤ P(S† ≠ S₀) + E[1_𝒜(1 − π₀(S₀))^{D_r}], where S† is the exact HPM over Ω.
  60|   - Production: max(n, p)·log₂(n+1)·π₀(S₀) → ∞ suffices, with no condition on mixing, the bridge or Ẑ.
  61| - **Lemma MR.** T12's identities (i.a)–(i.c) and (ii) hold given 𝓒, for bridge stages, terminal endpoints and the
  62|   pre-step states inside measured rounds. In particular E[W_r p̂_r(j) | 𝓒] = PIP_j for the coded RB recording. This is
  63|   the "mid-round extension" that ADJ_opus called unproved.
  64| - **Lemma ST.**
  65|   - Any π-invariant kernel leaves S₀ with probability ≤ o₁.
  66|   - All Gibbs coordinates together leave S₀ with probability ≤ o₁.
  67|   - One round leaves S₀ with probability ≤ (B+3)o₁ ≤ 19o₁.
  68| - **Theorem LT♯ (item b, Lemma LT corrected for the coded outputs).**
  69|   - Finite-sample bound: P(max_j|p̂_r(j) − 1{j∈S₀}| ≥ κ₀ + 2ε) ≤ δ/(εη) + λ₀/ε + P(W_r < η). Here κ₀ ≤ o₁ is attained
  70|     exactly, and λ₀ ≤ 19o₁.
  71|   - Weighted form: E[W_r‖p̂_r − 1_{S₀}‖_∞] ≤ g ≤ 21o₁.
  72|   - Consequences for endpoints, discovery, pooled pip_primary, MPM (strict ½ threshold) and the HPM.
  73|   - Asymptotically: posterior concentration (no rate) plus the non-collapse premise NC_r gives consistency of the coded
  74|     PIPs (sup-norm), MPM and HPM, for any N_e and any schedule. A vanishing-threshold variant is LT-e′.
  75|   - This fixes ADJ_opus Flaw 1 (RB values recorded mid-round, no factor p, no posterior-size control).
  76|   - Flaw 2 (the premise looks circular) is answered by labelling, not by removal. NC_r is computational:
  77|     - Theorem C discharges it;
  78|     - Theorem TR replaces it with a premise that involves no particle statistic;
  79|     - an observable condition certifies the finite-run event {W_r < η};
  80|     - no output certifies W_r ≥ η unless the store holds all of Ω;
  81|     - whether NC_r is necessary is **open**.
  82| - **Theorem C (concentrated bridge, item c).**
  83|   - For any grid, any T and any N_e ≥ 1: E|W_r − 1| ≤ β ≤ 2max{δ, (1−δ)o₀} ≤ 2δ̄, by telescoping (T-free). The same
  84|     bound holds for the pooled Ẑ/Z.
  85|   - Log-evidence tail: P(|log Ẑ − log Z| > u) ≤ β/(1 − e^{−u}).
  86|   - E‖pip_primary − 1_{S₀}‖_∞ ≤ 22δ̄; P(MPM ≠ S₀) ≤ 44δ̄; bias |E p̂_r(j) − PIP_j| ≤ β/2.
  87|   - So 1_𝒜δ̄ → 0, i.e. posterior concentration plus P-START, gives Ẑ/Z → 1 and consistency of the PIPs, MPM and HPM.
  88|     It gives O_P(r_n) rates when δ̄ = O_P(r_n), and NC_r holds.
  89|   - This improves the source's T²δ̄ condition.
  90|   - Label: the regime where the start already concentrates on S₀.
  91| - **Theorem TR (terminal repair, from BT1).**
  92|   - Every φ = 1 round kernel is minorised by π/M, with M = max π/π₀.
  93|   - For any island's bridge outcome: E‖p̂_r − 1_{S₀}‖_∞ ≤ g + (1 − 1/M)^L, and P(MPM ≠ S₀) ≤ 2(g + e_L).
  94|   - Posterior concentration plus P-OVL∞ (L/M → ∞ on 𝒜) gives consistency with no condition on Ẑ, the bridge or N_e.
  95|     In production this reads M = o_P(log n) on 𝒜.
  96|   - Label: a global-overlap condition relative to the executed burn-in, not certified by any output. For abstract
  97|     targets it is not nested with C's condition in either direction; whether coded targets separate the two is open.

  20| For k ≥ 1 the stage-k factor is q̂_{k−1}(e^{Δ_k d}) ≥ A_{k−1}e^{Δ_k d(s)}; multiplying over k = 1..t, Ẑ_{r,t} ≥ Z₀e^{φ_t d(s)}Π_{u<t}A_u, and
  21| Z₀e^{φ_t d(s)}/Z_t = q_t(s)/π₀(s). So W_t := Ẑ_{r,t}/Z_t ≥ (q_t(s)/π₀(s))Π_{u<t}A_u ≥ q_t(s)(1 − Σ_{u<t}x_u)⁺, and at t = T,
  22| W ≥ (π(s)/π₀(s))Π_{t<T}A_t. ∎(C-i)
  23| 
  24| ## Step 3 (C-ii, bridge occupation; T-dependent, kept as a separate statistic)
  25| 
  26| Fix u ∈ (0,1); put V_{−1} := 0 and V_t := Σ_{v=0}^{t}x_v for t = 0..T (C1 Astra #2); Y := Σ_{t=0}^{T}x_t1{V_{t−1} ≤ u}. Pointwise min(U, u) ≤ Y (if U ≤ u, Y = U; else with
  27| τ := min{t : V_t > u}, Y ≥ V_τ > u). On {V_{t−1} ≤ u}, Step 2 and Step 1 give W_t ≥ (1 − u)/(1 + δ̄), so
  28| x_t1{V_{t−1} ≤ u} ≤ ((1 + δ̄)/(1 − u))W_t x_t pointwise; MR-a with h = 1{S ≠ s} gives E[W_t x_t] = 1 − q_t(s) ≤ δ̄/(1 + δ̄).
  29| Hence E[Y] ≤ (T + 1)δ̄/(1 − u); with u = ½ and min(U,1) ≤ 2min(U,½): E[min(U, 1)] ≤ 4(T + 1)δ̄. (Only deterministic-index
  30| stagewise identities and a pointwise inequality; no optional stopping.) ∎(C-ii)
  31| 
  32| ## Step 4 (C-iii, T-free evidence bound; BT1 §1, re-derived)
  33| 
  34| Put a(S) := d(S) − d(s) and V_t := Ẑ_{r,t}/(Z₀e^{φ_t d(s)}) (V_0 = 1). Since Ẑ_{r,t} = Ẑ_{r,t−1}q̂_{t−1}(e^{Δ_t d})
  35| (`cpp/v3_engine.h:317-322`; W1-N1 Lemma B (B-a)),
  36|   V_t = V_{t−1}·q̂_{t−1}(e^{Δ_t a}).                                                               (1)
  37| *Rescaled MR-a.* MR-a at stage t − 1 with a bounded data-and-c-measurable f: E[Ẑ_{r,t−1}q̂_{t−1}(f)] = Z_{t−1}q_{t−1}(f) =
  38| m(∅)Σ_Sγ₀(S)e^{φ_{t−1}d(S)}f(S); dividing by the constant Z₀e^{φ_{t−1}d(s)} = m(∅)Z̄₀e^{φ_{t−1}d(s)}:
  39|   E[V_{t−1}q̂_{t−1}(f)] = Σ_S π₀(S)e^{φ_{t−1}a(S)}f(S).                                              (2)
  40| *Loss per stage.* With f_t(S) := (1 − e^{Δ_t a(S)})⁺ ∈ [0, 1] (bounded, admissible for MR), (1) gives
  41| (V_{t−1} − V_t)⁺ = V_{t−1}(1 − q̂_{t−1}(e^{Δ_t a}))⁺ ≤ V_{t−1}q̂_{t−1}(f_t) (since (1 − mean)⁺ ≤ mean of (1 − ·)⁺). By (2),
  42| E(V_{t−1} − V_t)⁺ ≤ Σ_Sπ₀(S)e^{φ_{t−1}a(S)}(1 − e^{Δ_t a(S)})⁺ = Σ_{S: a(S)<0}π₀(S)(e^{φ_{t−1}a(S)} − e^{φ_t a(S)}).
  43| Summing over t = 1..T telescopes (φ₀ = 0, φ_T = 1):
  44|   E Σ_t(V_{t−1} − V_t)⁺ ≤ Σ_{S}π₀(S)(1 − e^{a(S)})⁺ =: b₋.                                          (3)
  45| *Mean and deficit.* V_T = 1 − Σ_t(V_{t−1} − V_t) ≥ 1 − Σ_t(V_{t−1} − V_t)⁺, so E(1 − V_T)⁺ ≤ b₋. Let
  46| c := Σ_Sπ₀(S)e^{a(S)} = (Z̄₁/Z̄₀)e^{−d(s)} = π₀(s)/π(s) (because π(s)/π₀(s) = e^{d(s)}Z̄₀/Z̄₁). Then W = V_T/c
  47| (Z = m(∅)Z̄₁) and E V_T = c (E W = 1, MR-a at t = T with h ≡ 1). With b₊ := Σ_Sπ₀(S)(e^{a(S)} − 1)⁺, c − 1 = b₊ − b₋.
  48| Hence, using (c − V_T)⁺ ≤ (1 − V_T)⁺ + (c − 1)⁺,
  49|   E|W − 1| = 2E(1 − W)⁺ = (2/c)E(c − V_T)⁺ ≤ (2/c)(b₋ + (c − 1)⁺) = 2max(b₋, b₊)/c =: β.             (4)
  50| *Bounds on β.* The S = s terms of b₋, b₊ vanish (a(s) = 0). So b₋ ≤ Σ_{S≠s}π₀(S) = δ₀ and
  51| b₊ ≤ Σ_{S≠s}π₀(S)e^{a(S)} = c − π₀(s) = c(1 − π(s)) = cδ. With δ₀/c = δ₀π(s)/π₀(s) = (1 − δ)o₀:
  52|   E|W_r − 1| ≤ β ≤ 2max{δ, (1 − δ)o₀} ≤ 2δ̄.                                                         (5)
  53| Valid for every frozen grid (any T) and every N_e ≥ 1. *Pooled:* Ẑ/Z = ¼Σ_rW_r (CC3), so E|Ẑ/Z − 1| ≤ ¼Σ_rβ_r = β
  54| (β depends on the data only). *Log tail:* for u > 0, {|log(Ẑ/Z)| > u} ⊆ {|Ẑ/Z − 1| > 1 − e^{−u}}, so
  55| P(|log Ẑ − log Z| > u | 𝓒) ≤ min{1, β/(1 − e^{−u})}; the same islandwise. ∎(C-iii)
  56| 
  57| ## Step 5 (C-iv, coded PIPs, MPM, discovery, bias)
  58| 
  59| Let E_r := ‖p̂_r − 1_s‖_∞ and g := min{1, κ₀ + δ + (1 − δ)λ₀} (≤ 21o₁ by ST: κ₀ ≤ o₁, δ ≤ o₁, λ₀ ≤ 19o₁).
  60| `LT_theorem.md` Step 2′ gives E[W E_r] ≤ g. Since E_r ∈ [0, 1] and E(1 − W) = 0,
  61|   E E_r = E[W E_r] + E[(1 − W)E_r] ≤ g + E(1 − W)⁺ ≤ g + β/2 ≤ 21o₁ + δ̄ ≤ 22δ̄.
  62| *Pooled and MPM.* ‖pip_primary − 1_s‖_∞ ≤ ¼Σ_rE_r, so E‖pip_primary − 1_s‖_∞ ≤ g + β/2; MPM ≠ s forces this ≥ ½
  63| (`LT_theorem.md` Step 4), so P(MPM ≠ S₀ | 𝓒) ≤ 2(g + β/2) ≤ 44δ̄. No union over islands, no independence.
  64| *Discovery.* The N_e initial draws are evaluated (CC1): P(S₀ ∉ 𝓜_r | 𝓒) ≤ (1 − π₀(s))^{N_e} ≤ δ₀ ≤ δ̄.
  65| *Bias against the exact PIPs.* MR-c gives E[W p̂_r(j)] = PIP_j; so |E p̂_r(j) − PIP_j| = |E[(1 − W)p̂_r(j)]| ≤ E(1 − W)⁺ ≤ β/2
  66| (p̂_r(j) ∈ [0, 1] and E(1 − W) = 0), uniformly in j, and the same for pip_primary. ∎(C-iv)
  67| 
  68| ## Step 6 (C-v, asymptotic, joint law)
  69| 
  70| Assume 1_𝒜δ̄ → 0 in probability, i.e. 1_𝒜o₁ → 0 and 1_𝒜o₀ → 0 (localised concentration and P-START); P-CONC (global)
  71| plus P-START is sufficient, and only the localised form is used (LC2 issue 5). Integrating the conditional
  72| bounds truncated at 1 (bounded convergence): P(𝒜 ∩ {|Ẑ/Z − 1| > ε}) ≤ E[1_𝒜 min(1, 2δ̄/ε)] → 0; the log tail likewise;
  73| P(𝒜 ∩ {‖pip_primary − 1_s‖_∞ > ε}) ≤ E[1_𝒜 min(1, 22δ̄/ε)] → 0; P(𝒜 ∩ {MPM ≠ S₀}) ≤ E[1_𝒜 min(1, 44δ̄)] → 0; NC_r:
  74| P(𝒜 ∩ {W_r < ½}) ≤ E[1_𝒜 min(1, 4δ̄)] → 0; HPM: by PC and `D_theorem.md` §3, P(completed ∩ {Ŝ ≠ S₀}) ≤
  75| P(𝒜 ∩ {δ ≥ ½}) + E[1_𝒜 min(1, δ̄)] → 0. *Rates:* (W3-POST Theorem 1 (Rate), `Theory_work/Wave3/W3-POST/STATEMENT.md:79-80`, gives δ = O_P(r_n), hence
  76| o₁ = δ/(1 − δ) = O_P(r_n).) If 1_𝒜δ̄ = O_P(r_n) with deterministic r_n ↓ 0, the same bounds give,
  77| localised to 𝒜, Ẑ/Z − 1 = O_P(r_n), log Ẑ − log Z = O_P(r_n) and ‖pip_primary − 1_s‖_∞ = O_P(r_n) (probability rates, not
  78| L¹ rates under the joint law). Reported fields: Lemma PC. ∎
  79| 
  80| ## Remarks
  81| 
  82| - Honest label: the regime in which the start already concentrates (π₀(S₀) → 1 on 𝒜); the bridge has no mass to transport.
  83|   No rate for the start mass and no relation to the schedule length are needed (the locked v2 needed T·δ̄ → 0; the source
  84|   BLIND_fable Thm 4(b) needed T²δ̄ → 0). Valid for N_e = 1.
  85| - Linear dependence on δ̄ is *possible*: for N_e = 1, T = 1 a non-truth initial draw (probability δ₀) can give an O(1)
  86|   evidence error when d varies (if d ≡ 0 then W ≡ 1). No lower-bound family is claimed (SW1 #15).
  87| - The occupation sum U of C-ii genuinely grows with T (numerics: E min(U,1) → 1 at large T while W → 1); only the evidence
  88|   bound is T-free.
  89| 
  90| ## Numerical falsification
  91| 
  92| Falsification attempts; no violation detected (SW1 #25, #26):

  96|   budget, E|W − 1| ≤ β, β ≤ 2max(δ, (1−δ)o₀), E E_r ≤ g + β/2, bias ≤ β/2. Tolerance: 3 Monte Carlo standard errors; some
  97|   sample loss means exceed b₋ within that tolerance (the budget is nearly attained).
  98| - `numerics/RESULTS_v4.txt` (run_checks_v4.py, seed 404): **N fixed at 2**, T ∈ {1, 4, 32, 128}, two targets; loss ≤ b₋ and

   2|

   4| 
   5| Code of record: the production core on main, `Scripts/SMC_BVS/core/` (= commit 4676af6: `git diff --stat 4676af6 HEAD --
   6| Scripts/SMC_BVS/core` is empty). Paths below are relative to that folder. Line numbers are those of the working tree on
   7| 2026-11-09 (checked by `reviews/CITECHECK.txt` before the council).
   8| 
   9| **Relation to the N1 code of record.** W1-N1 used the frozen v2.2.1 core
  10| (`Scripts/Campaigns/2026-10-28_New_Campaign/code/core/v2_2_1/core/`). `diff --strip-trailing-cr` of the two
  11| `cpp/v3_engine.h` files shows only three differences: (1) main has **no plain-PIP accumulator** (`pip_plain`,
  12| `plain_acc`, `plain_round` removed); (2) `local_search` takes a `phase` argument (LS0); (3) comments. The elementary steps,
  13| the round, resampling and `draw_start` are byte-identical up to line shifts; `run_island_s` differs only by the removed
  14| plain-PIP accumulator writes, with no change to its statistical transitions, weights or evidence increments. `cpp/v3_ledger.h` differs only
  15| by the added phase `PH_LS0` and the removed registry hook. Other headers (SW1 #12; `diff --strip-trailing-cr` against the v2.2.1 tree, 2026-11-09): `cpp/v3_score.h`,
  16| `cpp/v3_util.h`, `cpp/v3_blocks.h`, `cpp/v3_calib.h` identical; `cpp/v3_start.h` identical up to and including `draw_pi0`
  17| (the text before `draw_pi0` and the function itself have equal SHA-256), its differences (from v2.2.1 line 181 on) being the
  18| start-mode / tie-aware DP used only by LS0; `cpp/v3_runtime.h` differs in 4 lines of `local_event` (event labelling for
  19| LS0). So every island-reachable sampler, table, scoring and start-draw function is unchanged, and N1's code bridge (W1-N1
  20| `lemmas/L1_bridge.md`) applies to main's island verbatim, **except** for its sentence identifying `pip_plain`; on main the only coded PIP is the
  21| Rao–Blackwell PIP.
  22| 
  23| ## CC1 — every π₀ draw is scored and reaches the ledger before its accept decision
  24| 
  25| - Initial draws: `cpp/v3_engine.h:286-292` — for each of the N particles, `draw_start(S)` (`:289`), `set_model`, then
  26|   `eval(P[i], ME_INIT)` (`:291`) with the default `emit = true`.
  27| - Independence proposals: `step_indep` (`cpp/v3_engine.h:182-192`) draws S ~ π₀ (`:184`), scores it with
  28|   `eval(tmpQ, ME_INDEP)` (`:186`, emit = true), and only then draws the accept uniform (`:189`) and accepts or not
  29|   (`:190-191`). A rejected proposal is therefore scored and emitted.
  30| - `draw_start` is `draw_pi0(st, *vs, S)` (`cpp/v3_engine.h:108`; `cpp/v3_start.h:158-176`): it consumes a
  31|   state-independent sequence of fresh uniforms of the island's stream (sizes, block sizes, submodels), a number that
  32|   depends only on the draw itself.
  33| - Counts: one round = the m = p + B + 2 labels in a random order (`cpp/v3_engine.h:195-214`); exactly one label is `I`
  34|   (`:211`), so every particle makes exactly one independence proposal per round. Per island: N_e initial draws; one round
  35|   per bridge stage t = 1..T (`:303-339`, `population_round` at `:331`); L burn-in rounds (`:343-347`); Hm = 4 measured
  36|   rounds (`:351-360`; `measured_rounds = 4L` at `v3_run.R:90`). Total exact π₀ draws per island:
  37|   **D_r = N_e(1 + T + L + 4)**; with `islands = 4L` (`v3_run.R:91`), D = 4·D_r for the final run.
  38| - The final islands run serially, island r on stream 9 + r (`cpp/v3_core.cpp:443-452`).
  39| 
  40| ## CC2 — the reported HPM is the hpm_better-maximum of every model scored in the final run
  41| 
  42| - `eval` (`cpp/v3_engine.h:89-101`): cache miss ⇒ scorer call, `fresh = true`, cache insert; then, if `emit`,
  43|   `led->event(..., fresh || !cache, ...)` (`:98-100`).
  44| - `Ledger::event` (`cpp/v3_ledger.h:104-113`): if `is_fresh`, `offer_stores` (`:112`) ⇒ `offer_hpm` (`:89-90`), which
  45|   replaces the running best iff `hpm_better(F, S, hpmF, hpmS)` (`:84-88`). `hpm_better` (`cpp/v3_util.h:121-126`) is the
  46|   strict total order: larger F, then smaller size, then lexicographic. F = log ϖ(|S|-model prior) + log m(S)
  47|   (`cpp/v3_engine.h:97`), so e^F ∝ π(S) on Ω and Σ_Ω e^F = Z.
  48| - Non-fresh events are idempotent re-visits: (a) cache hits — the cache is created empty for the final run
  49|   (`cpp/v3_core.cpp:409`) and is owned by it, so a hit means an earlier `eval` of the same model in this run; every
  50|   `eval` with `emit = true` that inserted it also offered it. The only `emit = false` call in the final run is the centre
  51|   of the final local search, `E.local_search(led.hpmS, ...)` with `emit_centre = false` (`cpp/v3_core.cpp:456`;
  52|   `cpp/v3_engine.h:382`), whose centre is the current running best and was therefore already offered. A cache clear
  53|   (`cpp/v3_score.h:284`) only causes a later fresh re-evaluation, hence a repeated (idempotent) offer. (b) `held`
  54|   (`cpp/v3_engine.h:103-105`) re-emits the particle's current state, which entered the particle through an `eval`.
  55| - Other offers: block tables (`cpp/v3_core.cpp:372-386`, `:408`; only |U| ≤ K, `cpp/v3_start.h:92`), inherited
  56|   calibration models (`cpp/v3_core.cpp:418-429`, size checked at `:425`), the final local search and LS0
  57|   (`:456`, `:476`), which use the same `eval`.
  58| - Reporting: on `status == "completed"`, `out$hpm <- led$hpm$model` (`v3_run.R:142`); otherwise the HPM is labelled
  59|   incomplete and no estimates are returned (`v3_run.R:143-149`).
  60| - Hence, on a completed run: **Ŝ = the hpm_better-maximum of 𝓜**, where 𝓜 ⊇ {all models evaluated by the final
  61|   islands} (in particular every π₀ draw of CC1). Since hpm_better ranks by F first, if F(S₀) > F(S) for every S ∈ Ω∖{S₀}
  62|   and S₀ ∈ 𝓜, then Ŝ = S₀ (CC5 gives 𝓜 ⊆ Ω).
  63| 
  64| ## CC3 — the coded PIPs, MPM and evidence
  65| 
  66| - RB recording: in a measured round, `step_gibbs` (`cpp/v3_engine.h:113-132`) computes o_j at the particle's current
  67|   state — the state immediately before its Gibbs-j step — as o_j = γ₁(S∪j)/(γ₁(S∪j) + γ₁(S∖j)) (`:124-126`, φ = 1), with
  68|   o_j = 0 when j ∉ S and |S| = K (`:116-119`, `oj` stays 0), and adds it to `rb_acc[j]` **before** the Gibbs uniform
  69|   (`:128-129`). `rb_on` is true only in the measured rounds (`:354-356`).
  70| - Island PIP: `res.pip[j] = rb_acc[j] / (N·Hm)` (`:364`), i.e. p̂_r(j) = (4N_e)⁻¹ Σ_{q=1}^{4} Σ_i o_j(Y^i_{q,j}).
  71| - `pip_primary = rowMeans(P)`, P = cbind of the island PIPs (`v3_run.R:159-162`): equal-weight mean over the 4 islands.
  72| - `mpm = orig[pip_primary > 0.5]` (`v3_run.R:163`), strict inequality.
  73| - `log_Z = log((1/R) Σ_r Ẑ_r)` by log-sum-exp (`v3_run.R:154`); `log_Z_r` per island (`:150, 153`); island Ẑ_r as in
  74|   N1 (`cpp/v3_engine.h:299` init, `:317-322` increments).
  75| - **No plain (endpoint) PIP is computed on main** (`grep -n plain` over `cpp/` and `*.R` finds only a comment).
  76| 
  77| ## CC4 — law of the draws (under H-U)
  78| 
  79| Under H-U (iid ideal U[0,1) uniforms U₁, U₂, … within stream 9 + r), let τ_k be the **number of uniforms already
  80| consumed** when the k-th π₀ draw of island r begins. τ_k is a stopping time of 𝓕_n := σ(U₁, …, U_n) (whether the k-th
  81| draw begins after n uniforms is determined by U₁..U_n). By the strong Markov property of an iid sequence,
  82| (U_{τ_k+1}, U_{τ_k+2}, …) is iid U[0,1) and independent of 𝓕_{τ_k}. The draw is a measurable function of this
  83| continuation (it consumes a number of uniforms determined by the draw itself, `cpp/v3_start.h:158-176`), so with START it
  84| is π₀-distributed and independent of 𝓕_{τ_k}, which contains the previous k − 1 draws. Hence the D_r draws of the
  85| potential island r are iid π₀ given 𝓒 (D_r is σ(𝓒)-measurable; SI). This is the indexing used by W1-N1
  86| (`Theory_work/Wave1/W1-N1/lemmas/L1_bridge.md:77-88`). Proof detail: `lemmas/D_theorem.md` §1.
  87| 
  88| ## CC5 — every model the ledger sees lies in Ω
  89| 
  90| Particles start in Ω (π₀ on Ω); Gibbs adds only if |S| < K (`cpp/v3_engine.h:116`); swaps preserve size
  91| (`:146-180`); proposals are π₀ draws; local search skips additions at size K (`:397`); tables |U| ≤ K
  92| (`cpp/v3_start.h:92`); inherited models checked (`cpp/v3_core.cpp:425`). So 𝓜 ⊆ Ω.
  93| 
  94| ## CC6 — the frozen grid length is at most T_e (production calibration only)
  95| 
  96| T_e = 4^e·max(1000, ℓ²), ℓ = ⌈log₂(n+p+1)⌉ (`v3_preprocess.R:23, 27, 30`). A constructed grid with more than T_e
  97| intervals is a failure (`cpp/v3_calib.h:94`); in the pilot schedule every non-terminal step advances φ by at least 1/T_e and the
  98| terminal step ends exactly at 1 (`cpp/v3_calib.h:32, 38-44`; the snap is toward 1), so in exact arithmetic it has at most
  99| T_e stages; the tier-1 fallback grid is either a successful construction or the pilot schedule
 100| (`v3_calib.R:122-124`). Hence on 𝒜, **1 ≤ T ≤ 4·max(1000, ⌈log₂(n+p+1)⌉²)**.
 101| 
 102| ## CC7 — B is bounded
 103| 
 104| B = min(⌊√n⌋, ⌊√p⌋, 16) (`v3_preprocess.R:22`), so the number of neighbour-swap labels per round is ≤ 16.
 105| 
 106| Note (SL1 item 3, LC1 issue 1): CC6 and the D_r lower bound concern production calibration. `v3_frozen` accepts any
 107| finite strictly increasing grid from 0 to 1 with no T_e ceiling (`v3_run.R:68-82`), and that grid reaches the engine
 108| (`cpp/v3_core.cpp:446`); but `v3_run_settings` always takes N_e and L from `setup$budgets` (`v3_run.R:88-92`), so
 109| `frozen$N`/`frozen$L` are not executed by the public wrapper. Arbitrary (N_e, L) are reachable only through the engine
 110| component `Engine::run_island(r, N_e, grid, L, 4, tier, nullptr)` (`cpp/v3_engine.h:269-273`); `init_states = nullptr` is required for the N_e initial π₀ draws (SW1 #13).

   8| Fix c ∈ A₀ (success set, index r ≤ R′) and run island r's potential record on an iid U[0,1) stream U₁, U₂, … (H-U).
   9| By CC1 the island makes exactly D_r(c) = N_e(1 + T + L + 4) calls of `draw_start` = `draw_pi0` (N_e initial draws; one
  10| independence proposal per particle per round; T + L + 4 rounds per particle). Order them by execution: k = 1, …, D_r.
  11| 
  12| Let τ_k be the number of uniforms already consumed when draw k begins, 𝓕_n := σ(U₁..U_n). Whether draw k begins after
  13| exactly n uniforms is a function of U₁..U_n (W1-N1 Lemma B (B-b): the control flow and the number of uniforms each
  14| operation reads are decided by values already read, the data and c), so τ_k is an (𝓕_n)-stopping time, finite since each
  15| operation reads a bounded number of uniforms (`L1_bridge.md:77-88`). By the strong Markov property of iid sequences,
  16| V^{(k)} := (U_{τ_k+1}, U_{τ_k+2}, …) is iid U[0,1) and independent of 𝓕_{τ_k}. Draw k equals Ψ(V^{(k)}) for the measurable
  17| map Ψ realised by `draw_pi0` (it reads 1 + (number of iterations of the remaining-size loop, which includes blocks assigned size 0) + (number of
  18| positive-size blocks) ≤ 1 + 2J uniforms (SW1 #9), a number determined by the values it reads, `cpp/v3_start.h:158-176`). By START, Ψ(V) ~ π₀ for V iid uniform.
  19| Draws 1..k−1 are 𝓕_{τ_k}-measurable (they end before draw k begins). Hence draw k ~ π₀ independently of draws 1..k−1, for
  20| every k: the D_r draws are iid π₀. Therefore P_c(no draw equals S₀) = (1 − π₀(S₀))^{D_r(c)} exactly.
  21| 
  22| Every draw is evaluated with `emit = true` before its accept decision (CC1), so each draw lies in 𝓜_r:
  23| {S₀ ∉ 𝓜_r} ⊆ {no draw equals S₀} and P_c(S₀ ∉ 𝓜_r) ≤ (1 − π₀(S₀))^{D_r(c)}.
  24| 
  25| *Freezing.* Augment the statistical record Φ(c, u) by the sequence of the D_r(c) π₀ draws: each draw is computed from
  26| (c, u) by the same control flow as Φ (W1-N1 Lemma B (B-0), (B-d)), so the augmented record Φ̃ is jointly measurable. Put
  27| g(c, u) := 1{no draw of Φ̃(c, u) equals S₀} for c ∈ A₀ and 0 otherwise; g is bounded and jointly measurable, and
  28| 𝓒 ⊥ U_r (SI), so by the T12 freezing lemma
  29| P(no draw of island r equals S₀ | 𝓒) = 1_{E₀}(1 − π₀(S₀))^{D_r(𝓒)} in the localised form. ∎(D-i)
  30| 
  31| ## §2 Several islands (D-ii)
  32| 
  33| Under IND-T, given 𝓒 the four streams are independent (and independent of streams 0–9), so the four indicator events
  34| {no draw of island r equals S₀} are conditionally independent given 𝓒 (apply the freezing lemma to the product
  35| g₁(c, u₁)⋯g₄(c, u₄) with (U₁..U₄) ⊥ 𝓒). Hence P(S₀ ∉ ∪_r𝓜_r | 𝓒) ≤ Π_r (1 − π₀(S₀))^{D_r} = (1 − π₀(S₀))^{4D_r}
  36| (D_r does not depend on r). Without IND-T only D-i is used. ∎(D-ii)
  37| 
  38| ## §3 The reported HPM (D-iii, D-iv)
  39| 
  40| *Deterministic step.* Let S† be the hpm_better-maximum of Ω (the exact HPM with the coded tie rule,
  41| `cpp/v3_util.h:121-126`; a strict total order, so S† is unique). By Lemma PC, on {completed}, Ŝ is the hpm_better-maximum
  42| of 𝓜 ⊆ Ω. If S† = S₀ and S₀ ∈ 𝓜, then S₀ is ⪰ every element of 𝓜, so Ŝ = S₀. Sufficient condition: δ < ½. Indeed then for
  43| every S ∈ Ω∖S₀, π(S) ≤ π(Ω∖S₀) < ½ < π(S₀), so F(S₀) > F(S) (e^F ∝ π on Ω, CC2) and S† = S₀. So
  44| {S† ≠ S₀} ⊆ {δ ≥ ½}.
  45| 
  46| *Probability.* {completed} ⊆ 𝒜 (no final run otherwise, `v3_fit.R` returns before `v3_final_run` when calibration
  47| fails). Hence
  48| {completed} ∩ {Ŝ ≠ S₀} ⊆ {S† ≠ S₀} ∪ (𝒜 ∩ {S₀ ∉ 𝓜_r}) for any fixed r ≤ 4,
  49| and by D-i, integrating over 𝓒 and the data (the conditional bound is ≤ 1),
  50| P(completed ∩ {Ŝ ≠ S₀}) ≤ P(S† ≠ S₀) + E[1_𝒜 (1 − π₀(S₀))^{D_r}] ≤ P(δ ≥ ½) + E[1_𝒜 (1 − π₀(S₀))^{D_r}]; with IND-T the
  51| exponent is 4D_r by D-ii.
  52| 
  53| *Production corollary.* Production budgets give N_e = 4^e·N₀ ≥ N₀ = max(2500, n, p) and L = max(4, ⌈log₂(n+1)⌉)
  54| (`v3_preprocess.R:24-25`, tiers `:30`; `v3_run.R:90`), and T ≥ 1 on 𝒜; so D_r ≥ N₀(1 + 1 + L + 4) = N₀(L + 6). ∎(D-iii)
  55| 
  56| *Asymptotics (D-iv).* P(S† ≠ S₀) → 0 (the MAP premise; implied by P-CONC since {S† ≠ S₀} ⊆ {δ ≥ ½}). (1 − a)^D ≤ e^{−aD}, so E[1_𝒜(1 − π₀(S₀))^{D_r}] ≤ E[e^{−Q}] with Q := D_rπ₀(S₀) on 𝒜 and Q := ∞ off 𝒜 (LC1 issue 2), i.e. the integrand
  57| 1_𝒜e^{−D_rπ₀(S₀)} is defined as 0 off 𝒜; it is bounded and → 0 in probability by P-OVL, so its expectation → 0 (bounded convergence). In production, D_rπ₀(S₀) ≥
  58| max(n, p)·(L + 6)·π₀(S₀) ≥ max(n, p)·log₂(n+1)·π₀(S₀), so the displayed deterministic condition suffices. ∎
  59| 
  60| ## Remarks
  61| 
  62| - D is a discovery statement: it does not say the particles or the RB PIPs are right (LT♯/C do that). Gibbs flips, swaps,
  63|   local search and LS0 only enlarge 𝓜, so the bound is conservative for the method; it is an equality for the draw
  64|   mechanism alone (`numerics/RESULTS_v1.txt` §5: 0.3754 vs 0.3728, 0.7876 vs 0.7861, z ≤ 1.07).
  65| - The equality concerns the potential run's D_r draws; a stopped run has fewer draws but reports no HPM as complete.

  35| ## Proof
  36| 
  37| **Step 1 (fixed c).** Fix c ∈ A₀ (the set of calibration values of L3, `L3_freezing.md:27-29`, whose pullback E₀ = {𝓒 ∈ A₀} ∈ σ(𝓒) is the
  38| localisation event; SW1 #21) and run the island on an
  39| iid stream U. By Lemma B (B-a, B-b) the run is T12's I(c) with N = N_e(c), M = 4, L′ = L(c), flag unset, and satisfies
  40| (R1)–(R3). Put f := h(·; c) : Ω → ℝ (bounded). Then:

  42| - (MR-b) is T12 (i.b) with the operation sequence "s rounds at φ = 1" (s ≤ L + 4; the coded terminal operations are
  43|   rounds, Lemma B (B-a)); s = 0 is (i.a) at t = T since q_T = π and Z_T = Z.
  44| - (MR-c) is T12 (i.c) applied to the post-terminal round number L + q with κ_i = κ(σ_i) := σ_i⁻¹(ℓ) − 1, a fixed function
  45|   of particle i's order alone (T12's own example, `STATEMENT.md:61`); X^i_{[κ_i]} is the state immediately before step ℓ,
  46|   which in the code is the state at which `step_gibbs`/`step_*` for label ℓ is entered (`cpp/v3_engine.h:205-212`).
  47|   The RB clause: for ℓ = G_j, f := o_j(·, 1) ∈ [0,1] (data-only), and π(o_j(·, 1)) = π(j ∈ S) because o_j(S, 1) is the
  48|   π-conditional probability of j ∈ S given S ∖ {j} (with value 0 when S ∪ {j} ∉ Ω, where π gives that configuration mass 0);
  49|   averaging over q gives T12 (ii) for p̂_r(j) = (4N_e)⁻¹Σ_{q,i} o_j(Y^i_{q,j}) (CC3).

  51| **Step 2 (measurability).** Each left-side integrand is g(c, U) for a function g on E × Υ defined, for c ∈ A₀ with the
  52| index in range, by g(c, u) := [Ẑ_t(Φ(c, u))/Z_t(c)]·(1/N_e(c))Σ_i h(X^{(t),i}(Φ(c, u)); c) (and the analogues with W and
  53| with Y^i_{q,ℓ}), and g := 0 otherwise. The record Φ(c, u) contains the stage-t population, the post-terminal populations,
  54| and every particle's order and within-round path (`L1_bridge.md:14-20`), so X^{(t),i}, X^{(s),i} and Y^i_{q,ℓ} =

   1| # Lemma PC — completed runs carry the potential island records
   2| 
   3| Status: PROVED-CHECKED (lemma checks LC1/LC2 Codex Sol; mid-point MP1 CONTINUE; sweep SW1 fixed; council C1 PASSED round 1 (gpt-6-astra 9.1, Claude Opus 5.5 8.8; all six gates PASS on both seats); C1 non-blocking edits applied). Text history: v1, 2026-11-09. Statement: STATEMENT.md v3 §2 "Lemma PC". Code paths relative to
   4| `Scripts/SMC_BVS/core/`. This is the limited comparison SL1 item 4 asked for, not the full GUARD-W audit.
   5| 
   6| ## Proof
   7| 
   8| Fix the data, a calibration value on 𝒜 and the final streams; assume EX-A.
   9| 
  10| (i) *Islands.* The only early return inside an island is the guard check after each bridge stage
  11| (`cpp/v3_engine.h:335-338`), which sets `res.partial = true`. In `cpp_final_run`, a partial island sets
  12| `status = "resource_limit"` and breaks the island loop (`cpp/v3_core.cpp:451`); later guard checks (final local search
  13| `:459`, LS0 `:480`) and any `NumericalFailure` (`:483`) also leave `status != "completed"`; nothing resets `status` to
  14| "completed". Hence on {completed} no island returned early: each island executed the whole of `run_island_s` (bridge
  15| `:303-339`, burn-in `:343-347`, measured `:351-360`). Under EX-A, the island's statistical record is a function of
  16| (c, island stream) only — the guard, clock, cache and ledger do not feed any transition, weight or evidence increment
  17| (W1-N1 Lemma B step (B-0), `Theory_work/Wave1/W1-N1/lemmas/L1_bridge.md`, valid on main by the CC header). The guard only
  18| decides *whether* to stop, and on {completed} it never stopped. So the record equals the potential (uninterrupted) record
  19| computed from the same stream; the same holds for the set 𝓜_r of models island r evaluated (incl. rejected proposals),
  20| which is a function of (c, island stream) through the augmented record of `D_theorem.md` §1 (C1 Opus #1).
  21| 
  22| (ii) *Reported fields.* On {completed}, `v3_assemble_final` skips the incomplete branch (`v3_run.R:143`) and sets
  23| `log_Z_r`, `log_Z` (`:150-154`), `pip_r`, `pip_primary`, `mpm` (`:159-163`) from the island results, which are the
  24| fields `logZ`, `pip` of (i) (`cpp/v3_engine.h:362-365`); these are the functions of §0 of the island records. `out$hpm` is the ledger's running best (`v3_run.R:142`); it is
  25| **not** a function of the island records alone (the records exclude rejected proposals, tables, inherited models, the final
  26| local search and LS0) — see (iii) (SW1 #1).
  27| 
  28| (iii) *Ledger.* Every model evaluated by island r goes through `eval` with `emit = true` (CC1–CC2), so it is offered to
  29| the HPM at its first evaluation in the run; the ledger lives for the whole final run (`cpp/v3_core.cpp:407`) and is never
  30| reset. So 𝓜 ⊇ ∪_r 𝓜_r (𝓜 also contains tables, inherited models, final-search and LS0 evaluations), 𝓜 ⊆ Ω (CC5), and by CC2
  31| Ŝ = the hpm_better-maximum of 𝓜. ∎
  32| 
  33| Consequence used downstream: for any event G about the potential island records (evidence, PIPs, MPM, particle states), {completed} ∩ G is the same as {completed} ∩
  34| G evaluated on the reported fields; so P(completed ∩ {reported error}) ≤ P(𝒜 ∩ {potential error}).
</file>

<file path="Theory_work/Wave3/W3-SAMP/lemmas/ST_stay.md">
   1| # Lemma ST — staying at S₀ under π-invariant kernels
   2| 
   3| Status: PROVED-CHECKED (lemma checks LC1/LC2 Codex Sol; mid-point MP1 CONTINUE; sweep SW1 fixed; council C1 PASSED round 1 (gpt-6-astra 9.1, Claude Opus 5.5 8.8; all six gates PASS on both seats); C1 non-blocking edits applied). Text history: v1, 2026-11-09. Statement: STATEMENT.md v3 §2 "Lemma ST".
   4| 
   5| Setting: fixed data, φ = 1, the labelled elementary kernels of T12 §1 (`Docs/Theory/proofs/T12_T8_frozen_run_identities/
   6| STATEMENT.md:25-31`): Gibbs G_j (j ∈ [p]), uniform swap U, B copies of the neighbour swap N, independence I. KERNEL: the
   7| coded steps realise these kernels (W1-N1 Lemma B; N9) and each is π-invariant (in fact π-reversible) at φ = 1 (T12
   8| "invariance", `PROOF_v6.tex:54-81`, as re-stated at `W1-N1/lemmas/L2_post_terminal.md:18-20`). S₀ ∈ Ω, π(S₀) > 0,
   9| o₁ = π(Ω∖S₀)/π(S₀).
  10| 
  11| ## (ST-a) Any π-invariant kernel leaves S₀ with probability at most o₁
  12| 
  13| Let K be a Markov kernel on the finite set Ω with πK = π. Evaluating at S₀:
  14| π(S₀) = Σ_S π(S)K(S, S₀) = π(S₀)K(S₀, S₀) + Σ_{S≠S₀} π(S)K(S, S₀).
  15| Hence π(S₀)·K(S₀, Ω∖S₀) = π(S₀)(1 − K(S₀, S₀)) = Σ_{S≠S₀} π(S)K(S, S₀) ≤ Σ_{S≠S₀} π(S) = π(Ω∖S₀), i.e.
  16| K(S₀, Ω∖S₀) ≤ o₁. ∎
  17| 
  18| ## (ST-b) The Gibbs family
  19| 
  20| T12 §1: at S, G_j moves to S⁺ = S ∪ {j} with probability o_j(S) and to S⁻ = S ∖ {j} otherwise, where o_j(S) =
  21| γ₁(S⁺)/(γ₁(S⁺) + γ₁(S⁻)) if |S⁺| ≤ K and o_j(S) = 0 otherwise. At S = S₀:
  22| - j ∈ S₀: S⁺ = S₀, so G_j leaves S₀ iff it moves to S₀ ∖ {j}, with probability 1 − o_j(S₀) = |o_j(S₀) − 1{j ∈ S₀}|; and
  23|   1 − o_j(S₀) = π(S₀∖j)/(π(S₀) + π(S₀∖j)) ≤ π(S₀∖j)/π(S₀) (|S₀| ≤ K so S⁺ = S₀ ∈ Ω).
  24| - j ∉ S₀: S⁻ = S₀, so G_j leaves iff it moves to S₀ ∪ {j}, with probability o_j(S₀) = |o_j(S₀) − 1{j ∈ S₀}|; if
  25|   |S₀| = K this is 0; otherwise o_j(S₀) = π(S₀∪j)/(π(S₀) + π(S₀∪j)) ≤ π(S₀∪j)/π(S₀).
  26| (γ₁ ∝ π on Ω.) So K_{G_j}(S₀, Ω∖S₀) = |o_j(S₀) − 1{j ∈ S₀}| ≤ π(S₀ ⊕ j)/π(S₀) (with π(S₀ ⊕ j) := 0 when S₀ ⊕ j ∉ Ω).
  27| The models S₀ ⊕ j, j ∈ [p], are pairwise distinct and different from S₀, so
  28| Σ_j K_{G_j}(S₀, Ω∖S₀) ≤ Σ_j π(S₀ ⊕ j)/π(S₀) ≤ π(Ω∖S₀)/π(S₀) = o₁. In particular κ₀ := max_j |o_j(S₀) − 1{j ∈ S₀}| ≤ o₁
  29| (and even Σ_j |o_j(S₀) − 1{j ∈ S₀}| ≤ o₁). ∎
  30| 
  31| ## (ST-c) One round
  32| 
  33| Hypothesis (stated in ST-c, SW1 #14): the round path law of T12 (R3), realised by the code under EX-A, H-U and KERNEL
  34| (W1-N1 Lemma B (B-b)).
  35| 
  36| Let a particle enter a round at φ = 1 in state X_{[0]} = S₀; the order σ (a bijection from positions {1..m} to the m labels,
  37| m = p + B + 2) has any law, independent of the entering state; given σ, the within-round path X_{[0]}, …, X_{[m]} is a
  38| Markov chain with kernels K_{σ(1)}, …, K_{σ(m)} (T12 (R3), `STATEMENT.md:44`; W1-N1 Lemma B (B-b)). Let
  39| E := {∃k ≤ m : X_{[k]} ≠ S₀}. On E let k* be the first such k; then X_{[k*−1]} = S₀. So
  40| P(E | σ) = Σ_{k=1}^{m} P(X_{[0]} = … = X_{[k−1]} = S₀, X_{[k]} ≠ S₀ | σ) ≤ Σ_{k=1}^{m} K_{σ(k)}(S₀, Ω∖S₀) =
  41| Σ_ℓ K_ℓ(S₀, Ω∖S₀) =: λ₀,
  42| the last equality because σ is a bijection, so each label occurs exactly once. Taking expectation over σ, P(E) ≤ λ₀.
  43| Bound λ₀: the p Gibbs labels contribute ≤ o₁ (ST-b); U, I and each of the B copies of N contribute ≤ o₁ each (ST-a, each
  44| is π-invariant at φ = 1). So λ₀ ≤ (B + 3)o₁, and B = min(⌊√n⌋, ⌊√p⌋, 16) ≤ 16 (CC7) gives λ₀ ≤ 19·o₁. ∎
  45| 
  46| Remarks. (1) No reversibility is needed, only πK = π for each label. (2) The bound is pathwise in the order and holds for
  47| every round at φ = 1, in particular the measured rounds, whatever happened before (the conditional law of the path given
  48| everything before the round is as stated; Lemma B (B-b)). (3) Equality in ST-b is what makes κ₀ the *exact* RB error of a
  49| particle sitting at S₀: its recorded value at G_j is o_j(S₀).
  50| 
  51| ## Numerical falsification
  52| 
  53| `numerics/RESULTS_v1.txt` §1: exact kernel matrices built from T12 §1 for three targets (incl. cap K = 2 and B = 2):
  54| Σ_j |o_j(S₀) − 1{j ∈ S₀}| equals the Gibbs leave-sum to machine precision and is ≤ o₁; every non-Gibbs label leaves with
  55| probability ≤ o₁; λ₀ ≤ (B + 3)o₁; the simulated mean leave fraction E[Λ] is ≤ λ₀. Invariance errors ≤ 1.1e-16.
</file>

   2|

   6| ## Setting
   7| 
   8| Fixed data. w(S) := π(S)/π₀(S); **M := max_{S∈Ω} w(S)** (≥ 1, since Σπ = Σπ₀ = 1); e_0 := 1 and e_L := (1 − 1/M)^L for L ≥ 1 (LC2 issue 4). S₀ ∈ Ω, δ, o₁,

  10| parameters and **any** bridge outcome.

  12| ## Statement
  13| 
  14| - (TR-a) For every order σ, the round kernel K_σ := K_{σ(1)}⋯K_{σ(m)} at φ = 1 satisfies K_σ(x, ·) ≥ M⁻¹π(·) for every x;
  15|   hence so does the round kernel K₁ (average over σ), and sup_x ‖K₁^L(x, ·) − π‖_TV ≤ e_L.
  16| - (TR-b) E[‖p̂_r − 1_{S₀}‖_∞ | 𝓒] ≤ g + e_L and E[1 − A_{r,q} | 𝓒] ≤ δ + e_{L+q} ≤ δ + e_L (q = 0..4).

  19|   Q → ∞ in probability; MP1 issue 1): for every ε > 0,
  20|   P(𝒜 ∩ {‖pip_primary − 1_{S₀}‖_∞ > ε}) → 0, P(𝒜 ∩ {MPM ≠ S₀}) → 0, P(completed ∩ {Ŝ ≠ S₀}) → 0 — with no condition on
  21|   Ẑ (NC_r not assumed), the bridge, N_e, or the grid. Production corollary: L = max(4, ⌈log₂(n+1)⌉), so P-OVL∞ means, localised to 𝒜,

  23| 
  24| ## Proof
  25| 
  26| (TR-a) *Independence kernel.* At φ = 1 the I step proposes y ~ π₀ and accepts with probability min{1, w(y)/w(x)}. For
  27| y ≠ x: K_I(x, y) = π₀(y)min{1, w(y)/w(x)} = min{π₀(y), π(y)/w(x)} ≥ min{π(y)/M, π(y)/M} = π(y)/M, using π₀(y) = π(y)/w(y)
  28| ≥ π(y)/M and w(x) ≤ M. For y = x: K_I(x, x) ≥ π₀(x) (the proposal x is accepted with probability 1) ≥ π(x)/M. So
  29| K_I(x, ·) ≥ M⁻¹π. *Round.* Fix σ and let k be the position of I; write K_σ = K_pre K_I K_post. Every elementary kernel is
  30| π-invariant at φ = 1 (KERNEL), so πK_post = π and K_σ(x, ·) = Σ_z K_pre(x, z)Σ_y K_I(z, y)K_post(y, ·) ≥
  31| Σ_z K_pre(x, z)·M⁻¹(πK_post)(·) = M⁻¹π(·). Averaging over the order law preserves the bound. *Doeblin.* Write

  34| ‖μK₁^L − π‖_TV ≤ (1 − 1/M)^L‖μ − π‖_TV ≤ e_L.
  35|

  49| E‖p̂_r − 1_{S₀}‖_∞ ≤ min{1, κ₀ + δ + (1 − δ)λ₀ + e_L} ≤ g + e_L. For the endpoints apply (TR-a) to K₁^{L+q} directly:

params.system:
You are an independent expert referee assessing the SHARPNESS of mathematical results in a research project on the
asymptotic theory of a sequential Monte Carlo method for Bayesian variable selection (linear regression, p <= n^A, often
p >> n). Every result is asymptotic; finite-n behaviour is not a defect. The project's main risk is publishing theorems
that are correct but weaker than what is achievable.

You receive the working files of one ticket and a list of headline claims located by file and line span. Ignore any
status, score or review verdict the files assert. Take each claim as correct; your job is NOT to re-check the proof.

For each claim assess:
(a) hypotheses: is any assumption stronger than the proof needs (say which weaker condition suffices, with the step
    where it is used), or is it necessary (give a counterexample or a known lower bound showing that)?
(b) conclusion: is the rate, constant regime, scaling range (e.g. the exponent range for p vs n, beta-min level, sparsity
    growth) or mode of convergence improvable? Compare with the best known results for Bayesian variable selection
    (e.g. Johnson-Rossell, Narisetty-He, Castillo-Schmidt-Hieber-van der Vaart, Yang-Wainwright-Jordan MCMC mixing,
    Song-Liang, Zhou-Yang-Chang-Liang); cite only results you are confident about, and say when you are unsure.
(c) the cheapest concrete route to a stronger version, if one exists, and how hard it looks.

Severity: SHARP = no improvement you can justify; IMPROVABLE-EASY = a stronger version follows with a modest change you
can describe; IMPROVABLE-HARD = a stronger version is plausible or known elsewhere but needs new work; UNCLEAR = cannot
judge from the material.

Output, in this order:
1. For each claim, a short section: claim id, the assessment (a)-(c) with exact locations (file:line).
2. Then exactly one line per claim, nothing after the last one:
SHARP <claim id> VERDICT=<SHARP|IMPROVABLE-EASY|IMPROVABLE-HARD|UNCLEAR>

  72| - `mpm = orig[pip_primary > 0.5]` (`v3_run.R:163`), strict inequality.
  73| - `log_Z = log((1/R) Σ_r Ẑ_r)` by log-sum-exp (`v3_run.R:154`); `log_Z_r` per island (`:150, 153`); island Ẑ_r as in
  74|   N1 (`cpp/v3_engine.h:299` init, `:317-322` increments).
  75| - **No plain (endpoint) PIP is computed on main** (`grep -n plain` over `cpp/` and `*.R` finds only a comment).
  76| 
  77| ## CC4 — law of the draws (under H-U)
  78| 
  79| Under H-U (iid ideal U[0,1) uniforms U₁, U₂, … within stream 9 + r), let τ_k be the **number of uniforms already
  80| consumed** when the k-th π₀ draw of island r begins. τ_k is a stopping time of 𝓕_n := σ(U₁, …, U_n) (whether the k-th
  81| draw begins after n uniforms is determined by U₁..U_n). By the strong Markov property of an iid sequence,
  82| (U_{τ_k+1}, U_{τ_k+2}, …) is iid U[0,1) and independent of 𝓕_{τ_k}. The draw is a measurable function of this
  83| continuation (it consumes a number of uniforms determined by the draw itself, `cpp/v3_start.h:158-176`), so with START it
  84| is π₀-distributed and independent of 𝓕_{τ_k}, which contains the previous k − 1 draws. Hence the D_r draws of the
  85| potential island r are iid π₀ given 𝓒 (D_r is σ(𝓒)-measurable; SI). This is the indexing used by W1-N1
  86| (`Theory_work/Wave1/W1-N1/lemmas/L1_bridge.md:77-88`). Proof detail: `lemmas/D_theorem.md` §1.
  87| 
  88| ## CC5 — every model the ledger sees lies in Ω
  89| 
  90| Particles start in Ω (π₀ on Ω); Gibbs adds only if |S| < K (`cpp/v3_engine.h:116`); swaps preserve size
  91| (`:146-180`); proposals are π₀ draws; local search skips additions at size K (`:397`); tables |U| ≤ K
  92| (`cpp/v3_start.h:92`); inherited models checked (`cpp/v3_core.cpp:425`). So 𝓜 ⊆ Ω.
  93| 
  94| ## CC6 — the frozen grid length is at most T_e (production calibration only)
  95| 
  96| T_e = 4^e·max(1000, ℓ²), ℓ = ⌈log₂(n+p+1)⌉ (`v3_preprocess.R:23, 27, 30`). A constructed grid with more than T_e
  97| intervals is a failure (`cpp/v3_calib.h:94`); in the pilot schedule every non-terminal step advances φ by at least 1/T_e and the
  98| terminal step ends exactly at 1 (`cpp/v3_calib.h:32, 38-44`; the snap is toward 1), so in exact arithmetic it has at most
  99| T_e stages; the tier-1 fallback grid is either a successful construction or the pilot schedule
 100| (`v3_calib.R:122-124`). Hence on 𝒜, **1 ≤ T ≤ 4·max(1000, ⌈log₂(n+p+1)⌉²)**.
 101| 
 102| ## CC7 — B is bounded
 103| 
 104| B = min(⌊√n⌋, ⌊√p⌋, 16) (`v3_preprocess.R:22`), so the number of neighbour-swap labels per round is ≤ 16.
 105| 
 106| Note (SL1 item 3, LC1 issue 1): CC6 and the D_r lower bound concern production calibration. `v3_frozen` accepts any
 107| finite strictly increasing grid from 0 to 1 with no T_e ceiling (`v3_run.R:68-82`), and that grid reaches the engine
 108| (`cpp/v3_core.cpp:446`); but `v3_run_settings` always takes N_e and L from `setup$budgets` (`v3_run.R:88-92`), so
 109| `frozen$N`/`frozen$L` are not executed by the public wrapper. Arbitrary (N_e, L) are reachable only through the engine
 110| component `Engine::run_island(r, N_e, grid, L, 4, tier, nullptr)` (`cpp/v3_engine.h:269-273`); `init_states = nullptr` is required for the N_e initial π₀ draws (SW1 #13).

   1| # Theorem D — draw discovery
   2| 
   3| Status: PROVED-CHECKED (lemma checks LC1/LC2 Codex Sol; mid-point MP1 CONTINUE; sweep SW1 fixed; council C1 PASSED round 1 (gpt-6-astra 9.1, Claude Opus 5.5 8.8; all six gates PASS on both seats); C1 non-blocking edits applied). Text history: v2, 2026-11-09 (v1 → v2: MAP premise S† = S₀ replaces δ < ½, BT1 §3.1).
   4| Statement: STATEMENT.md v3 §2 "Theorem D".
   5| 
   6| ## §1 The draws are iid π₀ given 𝓒 (D-i)
   7| 
   8| Fix c ∈ A₀ (success set, index r ≤ R′) and run island r's potential record on an iid U[0,1) stream U₁, U₂, … (H-U).
   9| By CC1 the island makes exactly D_r(c) = N_e(1 + T + L + 4) calls of `draw_start` = `draw_pi0` (N_e initial draws; one
  10| independence proposal per particle per round; T + L + 4 rounds per particle). Order them by execution: k = 1, …, D_r.
  11| 
  12| Let τ_k be the number of uniforms already consumed when draw k begins, 𝓕_n := σ(U₁..U_n). Whether draw k begins after
  13| exactly n uniforms is a function of U₁..U_n (W1-N1 Lemma B (B-b): the control flow and the number of uniforms each
  14| operation reads are decided by values already read, the data and c), so τ_k is an (𝓕_n)-stopping time, finite since each
  15| operation reads a bounded number of uniforms (`L1_bridge.md:77-88`). By the strong Markov property of iid sequences,
  16| V^{(k)} := (U_{τ_k+1}, U_{τ_k+2}, …) is iid U[0,1) and independent of 𝓕_{τ_k}. Draw k equals Ψ(V^{(k)}) for the measurable
  17| map Ψ realised by `draw_pi0` (it reads 1 + (number of iterations of the remaining-size loop, which includes blocks assigned size 0) + (number of
  18| positive-size blocks) ≤ 1 + 2J uniforms (SW1 #9), a number determined by the values it reads, `cpp/v3_start.h:158-176`). By START, Ψ(V) ~ π₀ for V iid uniform.
  19| Draws 1..k−1 are 𝓕_{τ_k}-measurable (they end before draw k begins). Hence draw k ~ π₀ independently of draws 1..k−1, for
  20| every k: the D_r draws are iid π₀. Therefore P_c(no draw equals S₀) = (1 − π₀(S₀))^{D_r(c)} exactly.
  21| 
  22| Every draw is evaluated with `emit = true` before its accept decision (CC1), so each draw lies in 𝓜_r:
  23| {S₀ ∉ 𝓜_r} ⊆ {no draw equals S₀} and P_c(S₀ ∉ 𝓜_r) ≤ (1 − π₀(S₀))^{D_r(c)}.
  24| 
  25| *Freezing.* Augment the statistical record Φ(c, u) by the sequence of the D_r(c) π₀ draws: each draw is computed from
  26| (c, u) by the same control flow as Φ (W1-N1 Lemma B (B-0), (B-d)), so the augmented record Φ̃ is jointly measurable. Put
  27| g(c, u) := 1{no draw of Φ̃(c, u) equals S₀} for c ∈ A₀ and 0 otherwise; g is bounded and jointly measurable, and
  28| 𝓒 ⊥ U_r (SI), so by the T12 freezing lemma
  29| P(no draw of island r equals S₀ | 𝓒) = 1_{E₀}(1 − π₀(S₀))^{D_r(𝓒)} in the localised form. ∎(D-i)
  30| 
  31| ## §2 Several islands (D-ii)
  32| 
  33| Under IND-T, given 𝓒 the four streams are independent (and independent of streams 0–9), so the four indicator events
  34| {no draw of island r equals S₀} are conditionally independent given 𝓒 (apply the freezing lemma to the product
  35| g₁(c, u₁)⋯g₄(c, u₄) with (U₁..U₄) ⊥ 𝓒). Hence P(S₀ ∉ ∪_r𝓜_r | 𝓒) ≤ Π_r (1 − π₀(S₀))^{D_r} = (1 − π₀(S₀))^{4D_r}
  36| (D_r does not depend on r). Without IND-T only D-i is used. ∎(D-ii)
  37| 
  38| ## §3 The reported HPM (D-iii, D-iv)
  39| 
  40| *Deterministic step.* Let S† be the hpm_better-maximum of Ω (the exact HPM with the coded tie rule,
  41| `cpp/v3_util.h:121-126`; a strict total order, so S† is unique). By Lemma PC, on {completed}, Ŝ is the hpm_better-maximum
  42| of 𝓜 ⊆ Ω. If S† = S₀ and S₀ ∈ 𝓜, then S₀ is ⪰ every element of 𝓜, so Ŝ = S₀. Sufficient condition: δ < ½. Indeed then for
  43| every S ∈ Ω∖S₀, π(S) ≤ π(Ω∖S₀) < ½ < π(S₀), so F(S₀) > F(S) (e^F ∝ π on Ω, CC2) and S† = S₀. So
  44| {S† ≠ S₀} ⊆ {δ ≥ ½}.
  45| 
  46| *Probability.* {completed} ⊆ 𝒜 (no final run otherwise, `v3_fit.R` returns before `v3_final_run` when calibration
  47| fails). Hence
  48| {completed} ∩ {Ŝ ≠ S₀} ⊆ {S† ≠ S₀} ∪ (𝒜 ∩ {S₀ ∉ 𝓜_r}) for any fixed r ≤ 4,
  49| and by D-i, integrating over 𝓒 and the data (the conditional bound is ≤ 1),
  50| P(completed ∩ {Ŝ ≠ S₀}) ≤ P(S† ≠ S₀) + E[1_𝒜 (1 − π₀(S₀))^{D_r}] ≤ P(δ ≥ ½) + E[1_𝒜 (1 − π₀(S₀))^{D_r}]; with IND-T the
  51| exponent is 4D_r by D-ii.
  52| 
  53| *Production corollary.* Production budgets give N_e = 4^e·N₀ ≥ N₀ = max(2500, n, p) and L = max(4, ⌈log₂(n+1)⌉)
  54| (`v3_preprocess.R:24-25`, tiers `:30`; `v3_run.R:90`), and T ≥ 1 on 𝒜; so D_r ≥ N₀(1 + 1 + L + 4) = N₀(L + 6). ∎(D-iii)
  55| 
  56| *Asymptotics (D-iv).* P(S† ≠ S₀) → 0 (the MAP premise; implied by P-CONC since {S† ≠ S₀} ⊆ {δ ≥ ½}). (1 − a)^D ≤ e^{−aD}, so E[1_𝒜(1 − π₀(S₀))^{D_r}] ≤ E[e^{−Q}] with Q := D_rπ₀(S₀) on 𝒜 and Q := ∞ off 𝒜 (LC1 issue 2), i.e. the integrand
  57| 1_𝒜e^{−D_rπ₀(S₀)} is defined as 0 off 𝒜; it is bounded and → 0 in probability by P-OVL, so its expectation → 0 (bounded convergence). In production, D_rπ₀(S₀) ≥
  58| max(n, p)·(L + 6)·π₀(S₀) ≥ max(n, p)·log₂(n+1)·π₀(S₀), so the displayed deterministic condition suffices. ∎
  59| 
  60| ## Remarks
  61| 
  62| - D is a discovery statement: it does not say the particles or the RB PIPs are right (LT♯/C do that). Gibbs flips, swaps,
  63|   local search and LS0 only enlarge 𝓜, so the bound is conservative for the method; it is an equality for the draw
  64|   mechanism alone (`numerics/RESULTS_v1.txt` §5: 0.3754 vs 0.3728, 0.7876 vs 0.7861, z ≤ 1.07).
  65| - The equality concerns the potential run's D_r draws; a stopped run has fewer draws but reports no HPM as complete.

   1| # Lemma PC — completed runs carry the potential island records
   2| 
   3| Status: PROVED-CHECKED (lemma checks LC1/LC2 Codex Sol; mid-point MP1 CONTINUE; sweep SW1 fixed; council C1 PASSED round 1 (gpt-6-astra 9.1, Claude Opus 5.5 8.8; all six gates PASS on both seats); C1 non-blocking edits applied). Text history: v1, 2026-11-09. Statement: STATEMENT.md v3 §2 "Lemma PC". Code paths relative to
   4| `Scripts/SMC_BVS/core/`. This is the limited comparison SL1 item 4 asked for, not the full GUARD-W audit.
   5| 
   6| ## Proof
   7| 
   8| Fix the data, a calibration value on 𝒜 and the final streams; assume EX-A.
   9| 
  10| (i) *Islands.* The only early return inside an island is the guard check after each bridge stage
  11| (`cpp/v3_engine.h:335-338`), which sets `res.partial = true`. In `cpp_final_run`, a partial island sets
  12| `status = "resource_limit"` and breaks the island loop (`cpp/v3_core.cpp:451`); later guard checks (final local search
  13| `:459`, LS0 `:480`) and any `NumericalFailure` (`:483`) also leave `status != "completed"`; nothing resets `status` to
  14| "completed". Hence on {completed} no island returned early: each island executed the whole of `run_island_s` (bridge
  15| `:303-339`, burn-in `:343-347`, measured `:351-360`). Under EX-A, the island's statistical record is a function of
  16| (c, island stream) only — the guard, clock, cache and ledger do not feed any transition, weight or evidence increment
  17| (W1-N1 Lemma B step (B-0), `Theory_work/Wave1/W1-N1/lemmas/L1_bridge.md`, valid on main by the CC header). The guard only
  18| decides *whether* to stop, and on {completed} it never stopped. So the record equals the potential (uninterrupted) record
  19| computed from the same stream; the same holds for the set 𝓜_r of models island r evaluated (incl. rejected proposals),
  20| which is a function of (c, island stream) through the augmented record of `D_theorem.md` §1 (C1 Opus #1).
  21| 
  22| (ii) *Reported fields.* On {completed}, `v3_assemble_final` skips the incomplete branch (`v3_run.R:143`) and sets
  23| `log_Z_r`, `log_Z` (`:150-154`), `pip_r`, `pip_primary`, `mpm` (`:159-163`) from the island results, which are the
  24| fields `logZ`, `pip` of (i) (`cpp/v3_engine.h:362-365`); these are the functions of §0 of the island records. `out$hpm` is the ledger's running best (`v3_run.R:142`); it is
  25| **not** a function of the island records alone (the records exclude rejected proposals, tables, inherited models, the final
  26| local search and LS0) — see (iii) (SW1 #1).
  27| 
  28| (iii) *Ledger.* Every model evaluated by island r goes through `eval` with `emit = true` (CC1–CC2), so it is offered to
  29| the HPM at its first evaluation in the run; the ledger lives for the whole final run (`cpp/v3_core.cpp:407`) and is never
  30| reset. So 𝓜 ⊇ ∪_r 𝓜_r (𝓜 also contains tables, inherited models, final-search and LS0 evaluations), 𝓜 ⊆ Ω (CC5), and by CC2
  31| Ŝ = the hpm_better-maximum of 𝓜. ∎
  32| 
  33| Consequence used downstream: for any event G about the potential island records (evidence, PIPs, MPM, particle states), {completed} ∩ G is the same as {completed} ∩
  34| G evaluated on the reported fields; so P(completed ∩ {reported error}) ≤ P(𝒜 ∩ {potential error}).
</file>

<file path="Theory_work/Wave3/W3-SAMP/lemmas/ST_stay.md">
   1| # Lemma ST — staying at S₀ under π-invariant kernels
   2| 
   3| Status: PROVED-CHECKED (lemma checks LC1/LC2 Codex Sol; mid-point MP1 CONTINUE; sweep SW1 fixed; council C1 PASSED round 1 (gpt-6-astra 9.1, Claude Opus 5.5 8.8; all six gates PASS on both seats); C1 non-blocking edits applied). Text history: v1, 2026-11-09. Statement: STATEMENT.md v3 §2 "Lemma ST".
   4| 
   5| Setting: fixed data, φ = 1, the labelled elementary kernels of T12 §1 (`Docs/Theory/proofs/T12_T8_frozen_run_identities/
   6| STATEMENT.md:25-31`): Gibbs G_j (j ∈ [p]), uniform swap U, B copies of the neighbour swap N, independence I. KERNEL: the
   7| coded steps realise these kernels (W1-N1 Lemma B; N9) and each is π-invariant (in fact π-reversible) at φ = 1 (T12
   8| "invariance", `PROOF_v6.tex:54-81`, as re-stated at `W1-N1/lemmas/L2_post_terminal.md:18-20`). S₀ ∈ Ω, π(S₀) > 0,
   9| o₁ = π(Ω∖S₀)/π(S₀).
  10| 
  11| ## (ST-a) Any π-invariant kernel leaves S₀ with probability at most o₁
  12| 
  13| Let K be a Markov kernel on the finite set Ω with πK = π. Evaluating at S₀:
  14| π(S₀) = Σ_S π(S)K(S, S₀) = π(S₀)K(S₀, S₀) + Σ_{S≠S₀} π(S)K(S, S₀).
  15| Hence π(S₀)·K(S₀, Ω∖S₀) = π(S₀)(1 − K(S₀, S₀)) = Σ_{S≠S₀} π(S)K(S, S₀) ≤ Σ_{S≠S₀} π(S) = π(Ω∖S₀), i.e.
  16| K(S₀, Ω∖S₀) ≤ o₁. ∎
  17| 
  18| ## (ST-b) The Gibbs family
  19| 
  20| T12 §1: at S, G_j moves to S⁺ = S ∪ {j} with probability o_j(S) and to S⁻ = S ∖ {j} otherwise, where o_j(S) =
  21| γ₁(S⁺)/(γ₁(S⁺) + γ₁(S⁻)) if |S⁺| ≤ K and o_j(S) = 0 otherwise. At S = S₀:
  22| - j ∈ S₀: S⁺ = S₀, so G_j leaves S₀ iff it moves to S₀ ∖ {j}, with probability 1 − o_j(S₀) = |o_j(S₀) − 1{j ∈ S₀}|; and
  23|   1 − o_j(S₀) = π(S₀∖j)/(π(S₀) + π(S₀∖j)) ≤ π(S₀∖j)/π(S₀) (|S₀| ≤ K so S⁺ = S₀ ∈ Ω).
  24| - j ∉ S₀: S⁻ = S₀, so G_j leaves iff it moves to S₀ ∪ {j}, with probability o_j(S₀) = |o_j(S₀) − 1{j ∈ S₀}|; if
  25|   |S₀| = K this is 0; otherwise o_j(S₀) = π(S₀∪j)/(π(S₀) + π(S₀∪j)) ≤ π(S₀∪j)/π(S₀).
  26| (γ₁ ∝ π on Ω.) So K_{G_j}(S₀, Ω∖S₀) = |o_j(S₀) − 1{j ∈ S₀}| ≤ π(S₀ ⊕ j)/π(S₀) (with π(S₀ ⊕ j) := 0 when S₀ ⊕ j ∉ Ω).
  27| The models S₀ ⊕ j, j ∈ [p], are pairwise distinct and different from S₀, so
  28| Σ_j K_{G_j}(S₀, Ω∖S₀) ≤ Σ_j π(S₀ ⊕ j)/π(S₀) ≤ π(Ω∖S₀)/π(S₀) = o₁. In particular κ₀ := max_j |o_j(S₀) − 1{j ∈ S₀}| ≤ o₁
  29| (and even Σ_j |o_j(S₀) − 1{j ∈ S₀}| ≤ o₁). ∎
  30| 
  31| ## (ST-c) One round
  32| 
  33| Hypothesis (stated in ST-c, SW1 #14): the round path law of T12 (R3), realised by the code under EX-A, H-U and KERNEL
  34| (W1-N1 Lemma B (B-b)).
  35| 
  36| Let a particle enter a round at φ = 1 in state X_{[0]} = S₀; the order σ (a bijection from positions {1..m} to the m labels,
  37| m = p + B + 2) has any law, independent of the entering state; given σ, the within-round path X_{[0]}, …, X_{[m]} is a
  38| Markov chain with kernels K_{σ(1)}, …, K_{σ(m)} (T12 (R3), `STATEMENT.md:44`; W1-N1 Lemma B (B-b)). Let
  39| E := {∃k ≤ m : X_{[k]} ≠ S₀}. On E let k* be the first such k; then X_{[k*−1]} = S₀. So
  40| P(E | σ) = Σ_{k=1}^{m} P(X_{[0]} = … = X_{[k−1]} = S₀, X_{[k]} ≠ S₀ | σ) ≤ Σ_{k=1}^{m} K_{σ(k)}(S₀, Ω∖S₀) =
  41| Σ_ℓ K_ℓ(S₀, Ω∖S₀) =: λ₀,
  42| the last equality because σ is a bijection, so each label occurs exactly once. Taking expectation over σ, P(E) ≤ λ₀.
  43| Bound λ₀: the p Gibbs labels contribute ≤ o₁ (ST-b); U, I and each of the B copies of N contribute ≤ o₁ each (ST-a, each
  44| is π-invariant at φ = 1). So λ₀ ≤ (B + 3)o₁, and B = min(⌊√n⌋, ⌊√p⌋, 16) ≤ 16 (CC7) gives λ₀ ≤ 19·o₁. ∎
  45| 
  46| Remarks. (1) No reversibility is needed, only πK = π for each label. (2) The bound is pathwise in the order and holds for
  47| every round at φ = 1, in particular the measured rounds, whatever happened before (the conditional law of the path given
  48| everything before the round is as stated; Lemma B (B-b)). (3) Equality in ST-b is what makes κ₀ the *exact* RB error of a
  49| particle sitting at S₀: its recorded value at G_j is o_j(S₀).
  50| 
  51| ## Numerical falsification
  52| 
  53| `numerics/RESULTS_v1.txt` §1: exact kernel matrices built from T12 §1 for three targets (incl. cap K = 2 and B = 2):
  54| Σ_j |o_j(S₀) − 1{j ∈ S₀}| equals the Gibbs leave-sum to machine precision and is ≤ o₁; every non-Gibbs label leaves with
  55| probability ≤ o₁; λ₀ ≤ (B + 3)o₁; the simulated mean leave fraction E[Λ] is ≤ λ₀. Invariance errors ≤ 1.1e-16.
</file>

  19|   Q → ∞ in probability; MP1 issue 1): for every ε > 0,
  20|   P(𝒜 ∩ {‖pip_primary − 1_{S₀}‖_∞ > ε}) → 0, P(𝒜 ∩ {MPM ≠ S₀}) → 0, P(completed ∩ {Ŝ ≠ S₀}) → 0 — with no condition on
  21|   Ẑ (NC_r not assumed), the bridge, N_e, or the grid. Production corollary: L = max(4, ⌈log₂(n+1)⌉), so P-OVL∞ means, localised to 𝒜,
  22|   M = o_P(log n) on 𝒜.
  23| 
  24| ## Proof
  25| 
  26| (TR-a) *Independence kernel.* At φ = 1 the I step proposes y ~ π₀ and accepts with probability min{1, w(y)/w(x)}. For
  27| y ≠ x: K_I(x, y) = π₀(y)min{1, w(y)/w(x)} = min{π₀(y), π(y)/w(x)} ≥ min{π(y)/M, π(y)/M} = π(y)/M, using π₀(y) = π(y)/w(y)
  28| ≥ π(y)/M and w(x) ≤ M. For y = x: K_I(x, x) ≥ π₀(x) (the proposal x is accepted with probability 1) ≥ π(x)/M. So
  29| K_I(x, ·) ≥ M⁻¹π. *Round.* Fix σ and let k be the position of I; write K_σ = K_pre K_I K_post. Every elementary kernel is
  30| π-invariant at φ = 1 (KERNEL), so πK_post = π and K_σ(x, ·) = Σ_z K_pre(x, z)Σ_y K_I(z, y)K_post(y, ·) ≥
  31| Σ_z K_pre(x, z)·M⁻¹(πK_post)(·) = M⁻¹π(·). Averaging over the order law preserves the bound. *Doeblin.* Write
  32| K₁ = M⁻¹π + (1 − M⁻¹)Q with Q a Markov kernel (Q := (K₁ − M⁻¹π)/(1 − M⁻¹) if M > 1; if M = 1 then π = π₀ and K₁ = π
  33| already). Since πK₁ = π, for any law μ: μK₁ − π = (1 − M⁻¹)(μQ − πQ), and ‖μQ − πQ‖_TV ≤ ‖μ − π‖_TV. Induction gives
  34| ‖μK₁^L − π‖_TV ≤ (1 − 1/M)^L‖μ − π‖_TV ≤ e_L.
  35| 
  36| (TR-b) Fix c. Work island by island: let 𝓗 be island r's own history up to the end of its bridge (stage-T round) and 𝓗′
  37| island r's history before its measured round 1 (conditioning on other islands' histories is not used; under SI alone it
  38| could carry information about island r's stream — SW1 #28). The displayed bounds are the averages of the conditional ones.
  39| For a particle, let φ_i := ¼Σ_{q=1}^{4}1{(q, i) bad} with "bad" as in `LT_theorem.md` Step 1 (enters round q away from S₀,
  40| or enters at S₀ and leaves during it). By (1) of `LT_theorem.md`, ‖p̂_r − 1_{S₀}‖_∞ ≤ min{1, κ₀ + (1/N_e)Σ_iφ_i}.
  41| *Per-particle chain.* By T12 (R3) (W1-N1 Lemma B (B-b)), given 𝓗′ each particle's subsequent rounds form a Markov chain
  42| with kernel K₁ started at its entering state (orders fresh and independent of the past); hence E[φ_i | 𝓗′] = ψ(X_i′), with
  43| X_i′ particle i's state entering measured round 1 and ψ(x) := E_x[¼Σ_q 1{round q bad}] ∈ [0, 1].
  44| *Stationary value.* Under X′ ~ π the entering state of every measured round is π-distributed (πK₁ = π); round q is bad
  45| with probability ≤ π(Ω∖S₀) + π(S₀)λ₀ = δ + (1 − δ)λ₀ (ST-c applies to a particle entering at S₀, whatever happened
  46| before). So π(ψ) ≤ δ + (1 − δ)λ₀.
  47| *Burn-in.* Given 𝓗, X_i′ ~ K₁^L(X_i^{(T)}, ·) (L rounds at φ = 1, R3), so E[ψ(X_i′) | 𝓗] = (K₁^Lψ)(X_i^{(T)}) ≤ π(ψ) + e_L by
  48| (TR-a), since ψ ∈ [0, 1]. Hence E[(1/N_e)Σ_iφ_i] ≤ δ + (1 − δ)λ₀ + e_L, and by concavity of min{1, ·},
  49| E‖p̂_r − 1_{S₀}‖_∞ ≤ min{1, κ₀ + δ + (1 − δ)λ₀ + e_L} ≤ g + e_L. For the endpoints apply (TR-a) to K₁^{L+q} directly:
  50| E[1 − A_{r,q} | 𝓗] = (1/N_e)Σ_i K₁^{L+q}(X_i^{(T)}, Ω∖S₀) ≤ π(Ω∖S₀) + e_{L+q} = δ + e_{L+q} ≤ δ + e_L (C1 Opus #3). These are bounded measurable functionals of the record, so the freezing lemma transfers them to
  51| "given 𝓒" in localised form (as in `MR_identities.md` Step 4). No weighting by W and no independence across particles are
  52| used.
  53| 
  54| (TR-c) ‖pip_primary − 1_{S₀}‖_∞ ≤ ¼Σ_r‖p̂_r − 1_{S₀}‖_∞; MPM ≠ S₀ forces this ≥ ½ (`LT_theorem.md` Step 4), so Markov gives
  55| 2(g + e_L). Every particle state was evaluated (CC1–CC2), so {S₀ ∉ 𝓜_r} ⊆ {A_{r,0} = 0} and P ≤ E[1 − A_{r,0}] ≤ δ + e_L.
  56| 
  57| (TR-d) e_L ≤ e^{−L/M}, so 1_𝒜e_L ≤ e^{−Q} → 0 in probability (Q as in P-OVL∞), and 1_𝒜g ≤ 21·1_𝒜o₁ → 0; integrate the truncated conditional bounds
  58| (bounded convergence). HPM via Lemma PC and `D_theorem.md` §3: P(completed ∩ {Ŝ ≠ S₀}) ≤ P(S† ≠ S₀) +
  59| E[1_𝒜 min(1, δ + e_L)] → 0, where S† := the hpm_better-maximiser of F over Ω and P(S† ≠ S₀) ≤ P(δ ≥ ½) → 0. ∎
  60| 
  61| ## Remarks (honest label)
  62| 
  63| - P-OVL∞ involves no final-particle statistic; it is a condition on (π, π₀) relative to the executed burn-in L (on (π, π₀)
  64|   alone once L is the production budget; MP1 issue 2). It is a **global overlap** condition: M is a
  65|   maximum over all of Ω, not computed by the method. Since M ≥ w(S₀) = π(S₀)/π₀(S₀), on 𝒜 P-OVL∞ forces π₀(S₀) ≥ π(S₀)/M, i.e. localised to 𝒜, π₀(S₀)·L → ∞ in probability under P-CONC (SW1 #11).
  66| - Abstract positive-target example (BT1 §2; **not** a realisation of the coded regression target — on a coded 3-state
  67|   space p = 2, K = 1 and d ≡ 0, so π₀ = π; SW1 #2): with π(s) = π₀(s) = 1 − ε, a second state of posterior mass ε/2 and
  68|   start mass εe^{−H}, M ≥ e^{H}/2 for any H. So, for abstract targets, start mass alone does not control M and the
  69|   conditions of C (π₀(S₀) → 1) and TR (M = o(L)) are not nested. Converse (abstract; C1 Opus #9): given π, M_n → ∞ with
  70|   M_n = o(L) and δ < 1, put π₀(s) := (1 − δ)/M_n and π₀(S) := c·π(S) for S ≠ s with c := (1 − (1 − δ)/M_n)/δ; then
  71|   w(s) = M_n, w(S) = 1/c ≤ 1 elsewhere, so M = M_n = o(L) while π₀(s) → 0. Whether coded regression targets separate them is open.
  72| - TR does not repair W: the evidence is not updated in the terminal rounds. In the "near" example
  73|   (`numerics/RESULTS_v1_sec4b.txt`) the PIPs are repaired while W stays collapsed.
  74| - Improves BLIND_astra2 Thm 5 in the concentrating regime: no log(p+1)/N_e → 0 condition and no union over coordinates.
  75| 
  76| ## Numerical falsification
  77| 
  78| `numerics/RESULTS_v3.txt` (run_checks_v3.py): exact minorization min_{x,y} K_σ(x, y)/π(y) ≥ 1/M for 200 random fixed orders
  79| σ on three targets (no violation); E‖p̂_r − 1‖_∞ ≤ min(1, g + e_L) by simulation. In the "near" case the tested bound is
  80| vacuous (min(1, g + e_L) = 1, M = 1.3e6): it shows repair **outside** TR's sufficient regime, not a validation of TR with
  81| collapsed W (SW1 #19). LC2's reviewer additionally enumerated all orders (up to 720) on 12 small targets.

You are an independent expert referee assessing the SHARPNESS of mathematical results in a research project on the
asymptotic theory of a sequential Monte Carlo method for Bayesian variable selection (linear regression, p <= n^A, often
p >> n). Every result is asymptotic; finite-n behaviour is not a defect. The project's main risk is publishing theorems
that are correct but weaker than what is achievable.

You receive the working files of one ticket and a list of headline claims located by file and line span. Ignore any
status, score or review verdict the files assert. Take each claim as correct; your job is NOT to re-check the proof.

For each claim assess:
(a) hypotheses: is any assumption stronger than the proof needs (say which weaker condition suffices, with the step
    where it is used), or is it necessary (give a counterexample or a known lower bound showing that)?
(b) conclusion: is the rate, constant regime, scaling range (e.g. the exponent range for p vs n, beta-min level, sparsity
    growth) or mode of convergence improvable? Compare with the best known results for Bayesian variable selection
    (e.g. Johnson-Rossell, Narisetty-He, Castillo-Schmidt-Hieber-van der Vaart, Yang-Wainwright-Jordan MCMC mixing,
    Song-Liang, Zhou-Yang-Chang-Liang); cite only results you are confident about, and say when you are unsure.
(c) the cheapest concrete route to a stronger version, if one exists, and how hard it looks.

Severity: SHARP = no improvement you can justify; IMPROVABLE-EASY = a stronger version follows with a modest change you
can describe; IMPROVABLE-HARD = a stronger version is plausible or known elsewhere but needs new work; UNCLEAR = cannot
judge from the material.

Output, in this order:
1. For each claim, a short section: claim id, the assessment (a)-(c) with exact locations (file:line).
2. Then exactly one line per claim, nothing after the last one:
SHARP <claim id> VERDICT=<SHARP|IMPROVABLE-EASY|IMPROVABLE-HARD|UNCLEAR>

  37|   **D_r = N_e(1 + T + L + 4)**; with `islands = 4L` (`v3_run.R:91`), D = 4·D_r for the final run.
  38| - The final islands run serially, island r on stream 9 + r (`cpp/v3_core.cpp:443-452`).
  39| 
  40| ## CC2 — the reported HPM is the hpm_better-maximum of every model scored in the final run
  41| 
  42| - `eval` (`cpp/v3_engine.h:89-101`): cache miss ⇒ scorer call, `fresh = true`, cache insert; then, if `emit`,
  43|   `led->event(..., fresh || !cache, ...)` (`:98-100`).
  44| - `Ledger::event` (`cpp/v3_ledger.h:104-113`): if `is_fresh`, `offer_stores` (`:112`) ⇒ `offer_hpm` (`:89-90`), which
  45|   replaces the running best iff `hpm_better(F, S, hpmF, hpmS)` (`:84-88`). `hpm_better` (`cpp/v3_util.h:121-126`) is the
  46|   strict total order: larger F, then smaller size, then lexicographic. F = log ϖ(|S|-model prior) + log m(S)
  47|   (`cpp/v3_engine.h:97`), so e^F ∝ π(S) on Ω and Σ_Ω e^F = Z.
  48| - Non-fresh events are idempotent re-visits: (a) cache hits — the cache is created empty for the final run
  49|   (`cpp/v3_core.cpp:409`) and is owned by it, so a hit means an earlier `eval` of the same model in this run; every
  50|   `eval` with `emit = true` that inserted it also offered it. The only `emit = false` call in the final run is the centre
  51|   of the final local search, `E.local_search(led.hpmS, ...)` with `emit_centre = false` (`cpp/v3_core.cpp:456`;
  52|   `cpp/v3_engine.h:382`), whose centre is the current running best and was therefore already offered. A cache clear
  53|   (`cpp/v3_score.h:284`) only causes a later fresh re-evaluation, hence a repeated (idempotent) offer. (b) `held`
  54|   (`cpp/v3_engine.h:103-105`) re-emits the particle's current state, which entered the particle through an `eval`.
  55| - Other offers: block tables (`cpp/v3_core.cpp:372-386`, `:408`; only |U| ≤ K, `cpp/v3_start.h:92`), inherited
  56|   calibration models (`cpp/v3_core.cpp:418-429`, size checked at `:425`), the final local search and LS0
  57|   (`:456`, `:476`), which use the same `eval`.
  58| - Reporting: on `status == "completed"`, `out$hpm <- led$hpm$model` (`v3_run.R:142`); otherwise the HPM is labelled
  59|   incomplete and no estimates are returned (`v3_run.R:143-149`).
  60| - Hence, on a completed run: **Ŝ = the hpm_better-maximum of 𝓜**, where 𝓜 ⊇ {all models evaluated by the final
  61|   islands} (in particular every π₀ draw of CC1). Since hpm_better ranks by F first, if F(S₀) > F(S) for every S ∈ Ω∖{S₀}
  62|   and S₀ ∈ 𝓜, then Ŝ = S₀ (CC5 gives 𝓜 ⊆ Ω).
  63| 
  64| ## CC3 — the coded PIPs, MPM and evidence
  65| 
  66| - RB recording: in a measured round, `step_gibbs` (`cpp/v3_engine.h:113-132`) computes o_j at the particle's current
  67|   state — the state immediately before its Gibbs-j step — as o_j = γ₁(S∪j)/(γ₁(S∪j) + γ₁(S∖j)) (`:124-126`, φ = 1), with
  68|   o_j = 0 when j ∉ S and |S| = K (`:116-119`, `oj` stays 0), and adds it to `rb_acc[j]` **before** the Gibbs uniform
  69|   (`:128-129`). `rb_on` is true only in the measured rounds (`:354-356`).
  70| - Island PIP: `res.pip[j] = rb_acc[j] / (N·Hm)` (`:364`), i.e. p̂_r(j) = (4N_e)⁻¹ Σ_{q=1}^{4} Σ_i o_j(Y^i_{q,j}).
  71| - `pip_primary = rowMeans(P)`, P = cbind of the island PIPs (`v3_run.R:159-162`): equal-weight mean over the 4 islands.
  72| - `mpm = orig[pip_primary > 0.5]` (`v3_run.R:163`), strict inequality.
  73| - `log_Z = log((1/R) Σ_r Ẑ_r)` by log-sum-exp (`v3_run.R:154`); `log_Z_r` per island (`:150, 153`); island Ẑ_r as in
  74|   N1 (`cpp/v3_engine.h:299` init, `:317-322` increments).
  75| - **No plain (endpoint) PIP is computed on main** (`grep -n plain` over `cpp/` and `*.R` finds only a comment).
  76| 
  77| ## CC4 — law of the draws (under H-U)
  78| 
  79| Under H-U (iid ideal U[0,1) uniforms U₁, U₂, … within stream 9 + r), let τ_k be the **number of uniforms already
  80| consumed** when the k-th π₀ draw of island r begins. τ_k is a stopping time of 𝓕_n := σ(U₁, …, U_n) (whether the k-th
  81| draw begins after n uniforms is determined by U₁..U_n). By the strong Markov property of an iid sequence,
  82| (U_{τ_k+1}, U_{τ_k+2}, …) is iid U[0,1) and independent of 𝓕_{τ_k}. The draw is a measurable function of this
  83| continuation (it consumes a number of uniforms determined by the draw itself, `cpp/v3_start.h:158-176`), so with START it
  84| is π₀-distributed and independent of 𝓕_{τ_k}, which contains the previous k − 1 draws. Hence the D_r draws of the
  85| potential island r are iid π₀ given 𝓒 (D_r is σ(𝓒)-measurable; SI). This is the indexing used by W1-N1
  86| (`Theory_work/Wave1/W1-N1/lemmas/L1_bridge.md:77-88`). Proof detail: `lemmas/D_theorem.md` §1.
  87| 
  88| ## CC5 — every model the ledger sees lies in Ω
  89| 
  90| Particles start in Ω (π₀ on Ω); Gibbs adds only if |S| < K (`cpp/v3_engine.h:116`); swaps preserve size
  91| (`:146-180`); proposals are π₀ draws; local search skips additions at size K (`:397`); tables |U| ≤ K
  92| (`cpp/v3_start.h:92`); inherited models checked (`cpp/v3_core.cpp:425`). So 𝓜 ⊆ Ω.
  93| 
  94| ## CC6 — the frozen grid length is at most T_e (production calibration only)
  95| 
  96| T_e = 4^e·max(1000, ℓ²), ℓ = ⌈log₂(n+p+1)⌉ (`v3_preprocess.R:23, 27, 30`). A constructed grid with more than T_e
  97| intervals is a failure (`cpp/v3_calib.h:94`); in the pilot schedule every non-terminal step advances φ by at least 1/T_e and the
  98| terminal step ends exactly at 1 (`cpp/v3_calib.h:32, 38-44`; the snap is toward 1), so in exact arithmetic it has at most
  99| T_e stages; the tier-1 fallback grid is either a successful construction or the pilot schedule
 100| (`v3_calib.R:122-124`). Hence on 𝒜, **1 ≤ T ≤ 4·max(1000, ⌈log₂(n+p+1)⌉²)**.
 101| 
 102| ## CC7 — B is bounded
 103| 
 104| B = min(⌊√n⌋, ⌊√p⌋, 16) (`v3_preprocess.R:22`), so the number of neighbour-swap labels per round is ≤ 16.
 105| 
 106| Note (SL1 item 3, LC1 issue 1): CC6 and the D_r lower bound concern production calibration. `v3_frozen` accepts any
 107| finite strictly increasing grid from 0 to 1 with no T_e ceiling (`v3_run.R:68-82`), and that grid reaches the engine
 108| (`cpp/v3_core.cpp:446`); but `v3_run_settings` always takes N_e and L from `setup$budgets` (`v3_run.R:88-92`), so
 109| `frozen$N`/`frozen$L` are not executed by the public wrapper. Arbitrary (N_e, L) are reachable only through the engine
 110| component `Engine::run_island(r, N_e, grid, L, 4, tier, nullptr)` (`cpp/v3_engine.h:269-273`); `init_states = nullptr` is required for the N_e initial π₀ draws (SW1 #13).

   1| # Theorem D — draw discovery
   2| 
   3| Status: PROVED-CHECKED (lemma checks LC1/LC2 Codex Sol; mid-point MP1 CONTINUE; sweep SW1 fixed; council C1 PASSED round 1 (gpt-6-astra 9.1, Claude Opus 5.5 8.8; all six gates PASS on both seats); C1 non-blocking edits applied). Text history: v2, 2026-11-09 (v1 → v2: MAP premise S† = S₀ replaces δ < ½, BT1 §3.1).
   4| Statement: STATEMENT.md v3 §2 "Theorem D".
   5| 
   6| ## §1 The draws are iid π₀ given 𝓒 (D-i)
   7| 
   8| Fix c ∈ A₀ (success set, index r ≤ R′) and run island r's potential record on an iid U[0,1) stream U₁, U₂, … (H-U).
   9| By CC1 the island makes exactly D_r(c) = N_e(1 + T + L + 4) calls of `draw_start` = `draw_pi0` (N_e initial draws; one
  10| independence proposal per particle per round; T + L + 4 rounds per particle). Order them by execution: k = 1, …, D_r.
  11| 
  12| Let τ_k be the number of uniforms already consumed when draw k begins, 𝓕_n := σ(U₁..U_n). Whether draw k begins after
  13| exactly n uniforms is a function of U₁..U_n (W1-N1 Lemma B (B-b): the control flow and the number of uniforms each
  14| operation reads are decided by values already read, the data and c), so τ_k is an (𝓕_n)-stopping time, finite since each
  15| operation reads a bounded number of uniforms (`L1_bridge.md:77-88`). By the strong Markov property of iid sequences,
  16| V^{(k)} := (U_{τ_k+1}, U_{τ_k+2}, …) is iid U[0,1) and independent of 𝓕_{τ_k}. Draw k equals Ψ(V^{(k)}) for the measurable
  17| map Ψ realised by `draw_pi0` (it reads 1 + (number of iterations of the remaining-size loop, which includes blocks assigned size 0) + (number of
  18| positive-size blocks) ≤ 1 + 2J uniforms (SW1 #9), a number determined by the values it reads, `cpp/v3_start.h:158-176`). By START, Ψ(V) ~ π₀ for V iid uniform.
  19| Draws 1..k−1 are 𝓕_{τ_k}-measurable (they end before draw k begins). Hence draw k ~ π₀ independently of draws 1..k−1, for
  20| every k: the D_r draws are iid π₀. Therefore P_c(no draw equals S₀) = (1 − π₀(S₀))^{D_r(c)} exactly.
  21| 
  22| Every draw is evaluated with `emit = true` before its accept decision (CC1), so each draw lies in 𝓜_r:
  23| {S₀ ∉ 𝓜_r} ⊆ {no draw equals S₀} and P_c(S₀ ∉ 𝓜_r) ≤ (1 − π₀(S₀))^{D_r(c)}.
  24| 
  25| *Freezing.* Augment the statistical record Φ(c, u) by the sequence of the D_r(c) π₀ draws: each draw is computed from
  26| (c, u) by the same control flow as Φ (W1-N1 Lemma B (B-0), (B-d)), so the augmented record Φ̃ is jointly measurable. Put
  27| g(c, u) := 1{no draw of Φ̃(c, u) equals S₀} for c ∈ A₀ and 0 otherwise; g is bounded and jointly measurable, and
  28| 𝓒 ⊥ U_r (SI), so by the T12 freezing lemma
  29| P(no draw of island r equals S₀ | 𝓒) = 1_{E₀}(1 − π₀(S₀))^{D_r(𝓒)} in the localised form. ∎(D-i)
  30| 
  31| ## §2 Several islands (D-ii)
  32| 
  33| Under IND-T, given 𝓒 the four streams are independent (and independent of streams 0–9), so the four indicator events
  34| {no draw of island r equals S₀} are conditionally independent given 𝓒 (apply the freezing lemma to the product
  35| g₁(c, u₁)⋯g₄(c, u₄) with (U₁..U₄) ⊥ 𝓒). Hence P(S₀ ∉ ∪_r𝓜_r | 𝓒) ≤ Π_r (1 − π₀(S₀))^{D_r} = (1 − π₀(S₀))^{4D_r}
  36| (D_r does not depend on r). Without IND-T only D-i is used. ∎(D-ii)
  37| 
  38| ## §3 The reported HPM (D-iii, D-iv)
  39| 
  40| *Deterministic step.* Let S† be the hpm_better-maximum of Ω (the exact HPM with the coded tie rule,
  41| `cpp/v3_util.h:121-126`; a strict total order, so S† is unique). By Lemma PC, on {completed}, Ŝ is the hpm_better-maximum
  42| of 𝓜 ⊆ Ω. If S† = S₀ and S₀ ∈ 𝓜, then S₀ is ⪰ every element of 𝓜, so Ŝ = S₀. Sufficient condition: δ < ½. Indeed then for
  43| every S ∈ Ω∖S₀, π(S) ≤ π(Ω∖S₀) < ½ < π(S₀), so F(S₀) > F(S) (e^F ∝ π on Ω, CC2) and S† = S₀. So
  44| {S† ≠ S₀} ⊆ {δ ≥ ½}.
  45| 
  46| *Probability.* {completed} ⊆ 𝒜 (no final run otherwise, `v3_fit.R` returns before `v3_final_run` when calibration
  47| fails). Hence
  48| {completed} ∩ {Ŝ ≠ S₀} ⊆ {S† ≠ S₀} ∪ (𝒜 ∩ {S₀ ∉ 𝓜_r}) for any fixed r ≤ 4,
  49| and by D-i, integrating over 𝓒 and the data (the conditional bound is ≤ 1),
  50| P(completed ∩ {Ŝ ≠ S₀}) ≤ P(S† ≠ S₀) + E[1_𝒜 (1 − π₀(S₀))^{D_r}] ≤ P(δ ≥ ½) + E[1_𝒜 (1 − π₀(S₀))^{D_r}]; with IND-T the
  51| exponent is 4D_r by D-ii.
  52| 
  53| *Production corollary.* Production budgets give N_e = 4^e·N₀ ≥ N₀ = max(2500, n, p) and L = max(4, ⌈log₂(n+1)⌉)
  54| (`v3_preprocess.R:24-25`, tiers `:30`; `v3_run.R:90`), and T ≥ 1 on 𝒜; so D_r ≥ N₀(1 + 1 + L + 4) = N₀(L + 6). ∎(D-iii)
  55| 
  56| *Asymptotics (D-iv).* P(S† ≠ S₀) → 0 (the MAP premise; implied by P-CONC since {S† ≠ S₀} ⊆ {δ ≥ ½}). (1 − a)^D ≤ e^{−aD}, so E[1_𝒜(1 − π₀(S₀))^{D_r}] ≤ E[e^{−Q}] with Q := D_rπ₀(S₀) on 𝒜 and Q := ∞ off 𝒜 (LC1 issue 2), i.e. the integrand
  57| 1_𝒜e^{−D_rπ₀(S₀)} is defined as 0 off 𝒜; it is bounded and → 0 in probability by P-OVL, so its expectation → 0 (bounded convergence). In production, D_rπ₀(S₀) ≥
  58| max(n, p)·(L + 6)·π₀(S₀) ≥ max(n, p)·log₂(n+1)·π₀(S₀), so the displayed deterministic condition suffices. ∎
  59| 
  60| ## Remarks
  61| 
  62| - D is a discovery statement: it does not say the particles or the RB PIPs are right (LT♯/C do that). Gibbs flips, swaps,
  63|   local search and LS0 only enlarge 𝓜, so the bound is conservative for the method; it is an equality for the draw
  64|   mechanism alone (`numerics/RESULTS_v1.txt` §5: 0.3754 vs 0.3728, 0.7876 vs 0.7861, z ≤ 1.07).
  65| - The equality concerns the potential run's D_r draws; a stopped run has fewer draws but reports no HPM as complete.
</file>

   2| 
   3| Status: PROVED-CHECKED (lemma checks LC1/LC2 Codex Sol; mid-point MP1 CONTINUE; sweep SW1 fixed; council C1 PASSED round 1 (gpt-6-astra 9.1, Claude Opus 5.5 8.8; all six gates PASS on both seats); C1 non-blocking edits applied).    4| vanishing threshold, from BT1 §4.1, §5, re-derived). Statement: STATEMENT.md v3 §2 "Theorem LT♯". Uses Lemma MR
   5| (`MR_identities.md`), Lemma ST (`ST_stay.md`), Lemma PC (`PC_completed.md`), CC3 (`CC_code_check.md`).
